Summer Olympic Games\n\nThe Summer Olympic Games are a big sports party that happens every four years. Many countries send their best athletes to run, swim, jump, and play games. The games are held in a different city each time. The first modern Summer Olympics were in Athens in 1896. The three best athletes in each sport get medals: gold, silver, and bronze. People all over the world watch the Olympics on TV and cheer for their favorite teams.
Diet (nutrition)\n\nA diet is all the food that a person eats every day. Different people and cultures choose different foods to eat. Long ago, people did a lot of hard work with their bodies. Now many people sit at desks or use machines, so they do not move as much. If they eat the same amount of food but move less, their bodies store extra food as fat. This can make them gain weight. Some people change what they eat to stay healthy or to lose weight. A person who helps others with their food choices is called a dietitian. Some people cannot eat certain foods because those foods make them sick. That is called a food allergy. Eating the right amount of the right foods helps people feel good and stay strong.
Barley\n\nBarley is a plant that looks like tall grass. It grows seeds that people and animals can eat. People use barley to make flour for bread and also to make a drink called beer. Barley is one of the oldest foods that people have grown.
Boiling\n\nBoiling is when a liquid gets so hot that it turns into a gas. This happens all through the liquid, not just on top. You can see bubbles form inside the liquid and rise up. When the bubbles pop at the top, the gas goes into the air. Water boils when it gets very hot, like in a pot on the stove. The temperature at which a liquid boils can change. If you go up a mountain where the air is thinner, water boils at a lower temperature. A pressure cooker makes the pressure higher, so water boils at a higher temperature and cooks food faster. Boiling is used to cook food, clean things, and make chemicals.
Toilet\n\nA toilet is a thing people use to get rid of body waste. Most toilets have a seat to sit on and use water to flush the waste away through pipes. Some toilets do not use water and are called dry toilets. A room with a toilet can be called a bathroom or restroom. Many homes have a toilet inside. Some toilets are outside in a small building called an outhouse. Public toilets are in parks or at big events like concerts. Some public toilets cost money to use. Toilets help keep places clean and safe.
Godavari River\n\nThe Godavari River is a very long river in India. It is the second longest river in the country. The river starts in a place called Trimbakeshwar and flows all the way to the sea. Many people think the river is special and holy. They go to the river to wash and pray. Every twelve years, there is a big fair called Pushkaram next to the river. The river helps plants and animals grow. It also gives water to many people.
Elephant\n\nAn elephant is the biggest land animal that lives on Earth. It has a very long nose called a trunk. The trunk is soft and can grab food, pick up things, and make loud sounds. Elephants also have big floppy ears that help them stay cool. Their skin is thick and tough. Baby elephants are called calves. A baby elephant drinks milk from its mother for two years. Elephants live in families and talk to each other with low sounds that people cannot hear. They eat grass, leaves, and branches. Some elephants have long teeth called tusks. People should not hurt elephants because there are not many left in the wild.
High jump\n\nThe high jump is a game where people try to jump over a long stick. The stick sits on two stands, and it is very high up. The person runs fast and jumps up to go over the stick without knocking it down. Each person gets three tries at each height. The high jump started in England a long time ago. Boys and girls both do high jumps in the big Olympic games. Some people jump backward over the stick, and that is called the Fosbury flop. Others jump like scissors, and that is called the scissor kick.
Ocean sunfish\n\nThe ocean sunfish is a very big fish that lives in warm oceans. It is the heaviest fish with bones in the world. Its body is round and flat, like a big pancake. It does not have a tail like most fish. Instead, it flaps its long top and bottom fins to swim. Sometimes it floats on its side at the top of the water to get warm from the sun. It eats jellyfish, small fish, and other sea animals. Its skin can be silver or white, and it can change color when it is scared.
San Salvador\n\nSan Salvador is the biggest city and the capital of a country called El Salvador. Many important buildings are there, like where the president lives and where leaders make laws. The city is up high in the mountains and has volcanoes all around. Sometimes the ground shakes because of earthquakes. Many people live in San Salvador, and big games and shows happen there.
Space Shuttle\n\nA Space Shuttle is a big machine that NASA used to fly people and things into space. It looked like a big airplane with wings and a tail. The Space Shuttle could be used many times, unlike other spacecraft that could only be used once. It had three parts: the orbiter (the part that looked like a plane), a big orange fuel tank, and two long white rocket boosters on the sides. The orbiter carried astronauts and cargo like satellites or parts of a space station. When the Shuttle came back to Earth, it glided like a plane and landed on a runway. The Space Shuttle helped build the International Space Station and fix the Hubble telescope. Now the Space Shuttles are in museums where people can see them.
Concussion\n\nA concussion is a hurt inside your head that happens when you get hit on the head. It can make your brain get bumped. You might get a headache or feel dizzy. Some people feel very tired or have trouble seeing. You might feel confused or even fall asleep for a little while. If you hit your head hard, a doctor should check you. Wearing a helmet when you ride a bike or play sports can help keep your head safe.
Forgiveness\n\nForgiveness is when you decide not to be mad at someone who did something wrong. You stop being angry and stop wanting to get back at them. It is a choice you make inside your heart. When you forgive, you let go of bad feelings. You can forgive someone even if they do not say sorry. Many people around the world believe forgiveness is important. It helps you feel happy and peaceful inside.
Suriname\n\nSuriname is a country in South America. It is between Guyana and French Guiana. The capital city is Paramaribo, where almost half of the people live. About half a million people live in Suriname. The country used to be part of the Netherlands and became its own country in 1975. Many people there speak Dutch. The country has big forests and many rivers. People in Suriname work on farms, grow sugar, and find gold and oil in the ground. Children go to school until they are twelve years old.
Comoros\n\nComoros is a small country made of islands in the Indian Ocean. It is between Madagascar and Africa. The islands are from volcanoes. The biggest island is Grande Comore. The capital city is Moroni. The weather is warm most of the year. It rains a lot from December to April. The country is one of the poorest in the world. Many people grow food and fish for a living. Comoros grows a lot of vanilla and a flower called ylang-ylang.
Beech\n\nA beech is a big tree that grows in Europe, Asia, and North America. It has smooth, light gray bark. In spring, the tree grows small flowers and new leaves. The fruit of the beech is a small nut called a beechnut. You can eat the nuts, but they taste a little bitter. Beech trees make a lot of shade, so not many plants grow under them. People use beech wood to make furniture, tools, and kitchen things. The wood is white or light red and burns well for fire.
Joint\n\nA joint is the place where two or more bones meet. Joints help your body move, like when you bend your elbow or knee. Between the bones there is a soft cushion called cartilage that helps the bones slide smoothly. Some joints have a little bag of slippery fluid that works like a cushion between bones and muscles. This fluid helps the joint move without rubbing too much.
Great Barrier Reef\n\nThe Great Barrier Reef is the biggest coral reef in the world. It is near Australia in the ocean. It is made of many small animals called corals. The reef is so big that people can see it from space. Many fish, turtles, whales, and birds live there. There are over 1,500 kinds of fish. The reef is very old, but it is in danger. When the water gets too warm, the corals lose their color and can die. People are trying to keep the reef safe.
National anthem\n\nA national anthem is a special song for a country. People sing it to show they love their country. Most countries have a national anthem. Some countries also have a special song for their king or queen.
Cheetah\n\nA cheetah is a big cat that lives in Africa and a few in Iran. It is the fastest animal on land and can run very fast, faster than a car. Cheetahs have long thin legs and a long spotted tail to help them run. They hunt in the early morning or late evening. They eat animals like gazelles and hares. When a cheetah hunts, it sneaks close and then runs very fast to catch its food. Cheetahs cannot fight lions or hyenas, so they eat quickly. A mother cheetah has about 3 to 5 babies called cubs. The cubs stay with their mom for two years to learn how to hunt. Cheetahs do not attack people.
Artist\n\nAn artist is a person who makes art. Art can be a drawing, a painting, a song, a dance, or a story. Some artists use paint and brushes to make pictures. Other artists sing or play music. Some artists act in plays or movies. An artist uses their hands and ideas to make something beautiful. You can be an artist too when you draw or make something.
Adhesive\n\nAn adhesive is something that sticks two things together. Glue is an adhesive. Sticky tape is an adhesive. Some adhesives come from plants or animals. Others are made by people. You can use glue to stick paper. Sticky notes have a special glue that lets you take them off again. Some glues are very strong and hold big things together, like furniture.
Baseball\n\nBaseball is a game played by two teams on a big field. One team throws a small round ball, and the other team tries to hit it with a bat. If you hit the ball, you run to touch four safe spots called bases. You get a point, called a run, when you run all the way around the bases and back to where you started. The other team tries to catch the ball or tag you with it to get you out. After three outs, the teams switch places. The team with the most runs wins. Baseball started in the United States a long time ago. Many people in the United States and Japan love to play and watch baseball.
Tokyo\n\nTokyo is the biggest city in Japan and the capital. It is on an island called Honshu. Many people live and work there. Tokyo has tall buildings, trains, and busy streets. The emperor of Japan lives in a big palace in Tokyo, but people cannot go inside. Long ago, Tokyo was called Edo and was a small fishing village. It grew into a big city. Tokyo was hurt by a big earthquake in 1923 and by bombs in a war. After the war, people built it again. Now Tokyo has many fun places to see, like Tokyo Tower and Tokyo Skytree. There are also old temples and parks. Many trains and subways help people move around the city.
Ore\n\nAn ore is a special kind of rock that has a metal inside it. People dig up ores from the ground in mines. Sometimes you can find ores on the ground outside. To get the metal out, the ore is heated in a very hot oven. For example, iron ore is heated in a big furnace to make iron.
Igloo\n\nAn igloo is a little house made of snow blocks. People build it by stacking snow bricks on top of each other in a round shape like half a ball. The igloo keeps people warm and dry inside. Hunters used igloos when they were far from home in the winter. You can find igloos in very cold places like Canada and Greenland. The Inuit people are very good at building igloos. Sometimes they build big igloos where many people can sit together or even dance.
Sweet potato\n\nA sweet potato is a plant that grows a root you can eat. The root is sweet and soft when cooked. It has a lot of fiber and something called beta-carotene, which is good for your body. People eat sweet potatoes all over the world. They can be orange, purple, or red on the inside. You can bake them, boil them, or make them into fries. Sweet potatoes are not the same as regular potatoes, but they look a little alike.
Sushi\n\nSushi is a food that comes from Japan. It is made with special rice that has vinegar, salt, and sugar mixed in. Sushi often has raw or cooked fish on top or inside. Sometimes it has vegetables or meat instead of fish. Some sushi is wrapped in a thin sheet of seaweed called nori. People eat sushi with soy sauce and wasabi. You can eat sushi with your hands or with chopsticks. There are many kinds of sushi. One kind has fish on top of a small ball of rice. Another kind has rice and fish rolled up inside seaweed. In Japan, some sushi shops have plates of sushi on a moving belt. People pick the plates they want as they go by. Sushi is now popular in many countries around the world.
Saw\n\nA saw is a tool that cuts things. Some saws are hand tools that you push or pull with your arm. Other saws use electricity or a motor to move. A chainsaw is a powerful saw used to cut down trees. A circular saw has a round blade that spins very fast. A jig saw moves its blade up and down to make curved cuts. Saws have sharp teeth, so they can be dangerous. You have to be careful not to touch the sharp edges. Using a saw is usually noisy.
Freighter\n\nA freighter is a big boat that carries things from one place to another. It moves boxes, food, toys, and other stuff across the ocean. Many freighters travel on the sea every day. They have big cranes to pick up and put down the heavy boxes. Some freighters are very small, and some are huge.
Odor\n\nAn odor is a smell that you can pick up with your nose. Some smells are nice, like flowers or cookies baking. Other smells are not nice, like garbage or stinky socks. Your nose can tell the difference between many different smells. Animals also use smells to talk to each other. For example, a mother bee can send out a smell to tell other bees where to go. Some smells are so strong that you can smell them from far away.
Rigel\n\nRigel is a very big, hot star in the sky. It is part of a group of stars called Orion. Rigel is much bigger and brighter than our Sun. It looks like a small blue-white dot on clear nights. Rigel is actually four stars that stay close together. It will use up its fuel and one day explode.
Finger\n\nA finger is a part of your hand. You have five fingers on each hand. The first one is called the thumb. Then comes the index finger, the middle finger, the ring finger, and the little finger. Some people call the little finger a pinky. Fingers help you pick up toys, hold a crayon, and wave hello. Each finger has small bones inside that let it bend.
Thesaurus\n\nA thesaurus is a special book or list that helps you find other words that mean the same thing. For example, if you look up the word "big," a thesaurus shows you words like "huge" and "large." Some thesauruses also show words that mean the opposite, like "small." People use a thesaurus when they write stories or papers to find better words.
Watermill\n\nA watermill is a machine that uses moving water to do work. Water pushes a big wheel or a special fan called a turbine. The wheel turns and makes other parts move. Long ago, people used watermills to grind grain into flour for bread. They also used watermills to cut wood or shape metal. Watermills were built near rivers or streams. The water flows through a channel to the wheel. Then the water leaves through another channel. Some watermills have a wheel that lies flat, and some have a wheel that stands up straight. Watermills helped people do hard work without using their own strength.
Lungfish\n\nA lungfish is a special kind of fish that lives in fresh water. It has both lungs and gills, so it can breathe air and water. Lungfish live in small lakes and rivers that sometimes dry up. When the water goes away, the lungfish can stay alive in the mud for a very long time, even up to four years. It uses its lungs to breathe while it sleeps in the mud. There are eight kinds of lungfish. Most live in Africa, and one lives in South America and one in Australia.
Altruism\n\nAltruism is when you help someone else without wanting anything back. It means doing something nice just for the other person, like sharing a toy or giving a hug. You might give up your time or something you have, but you don't expect a reward. It is the opposite of being selfish. Many people think it is good to be kind to others. Some scientists say that animals also help each other, like when a bird warns its friends about danger. Religions like Buddhism and Christianity teach that helping others is important.
Commerce\n\nCommerce is when people buy and sell things. It is like a big store where you can get toys, food, or clothes. Some people sell cars, and some sell things on the computer. Commerce can happen between towns or even between different countries.
Mummification\n\nMummification is a way to keep a dead body from rotting. The skin and muscles dry out and look like old leather. Long ago in Egypt, people made mummies on purpose. They believed the body needed to stay whole for a next life. They took out the soft parts inside, dried the body with salt, and wrapped it in cloth bandages. This took about 70 days. They also made mummies of cats, dogs, and birds. Some mummies happen by themselves in very dry, cold, or hot places. Mummies have been found all over the world.
History of Europe\n\nThe history of Europe is the story of all the people who lived in Europe long ago up to today. A long time ago, there were people called the Greeks and the Romans. The Romans had a big empire, but it fell apart. Then there was a time called the Middle Ages, when knights lived in castles and the Black Death made many people sick. Later, people discovered new lands across the ocean, like America. There were big wars, like World War I and World War II. After that, Europe was split into two parts: one part where people could vote and one part where the government told everyone what to do. In 1989, the Berlin Wall came down, and many countries joined together to make the European Union.
Angola\n\nAngola is a country in Africa. It is on the west side of Africa, next to the Atlantic Ocean. The big ocean touches its coast. Angola shares borders with Namibia, Zambia, and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The capital city is Luanda. Many people live there. Angola has a hot rainy season and a dry season. The country is very big, the seventh largest in Africa.
Thought experiment\n\nA thought experiment is a pretend experiment that happens in your mind, not in a real room. You do not need any tools or toys. You just think about a question like "what would happen if...?" and try to guess the answer. Scientists and smart people use thought experiments to learn new things. Anyone can do a thought experiment by using their imagination.
Mandolin\n\nA mandolin is a musical instrument that you play by hitting its strings. It has eight strings and a body made of wood. The mandolin sounds a little like a violin. People hold it and hit the strings to make music.
Harbor\n\nA harbor is a safe place in the water where big boats called ships can rest. Some harbors have docks where ships stop to drop off or pick up things. People use trucks and trains to move those things to other places. A harbor can be made by nature, like a bay, or built by people, like a special wall in the water.
Zambia\n\nZambia is a country in Africa. It is in the southern part of Africa. Zambia shares its land with many other countries. The capital city is Lusaka, and it is the biggest city in Zambia. The country is named after the Zambezi River. Zambia has a big waterfall called Victoria Falls, which is one of the most famous waterfalls in the world. People in Zambia speak many different languages, but the main language is English. Zambia used to be called Northern Rhodesia. It became its own country on October 24, 1964. The first leader was Kenneth Kaunda. Now, the people vote for their leader. The current leader is Hakainde Hichilema. Zambia has a lot of copper, which is a metal that people dig out of the ground. Selling copper helps the country get money.
Civil law\n\nCivil law is a set of rules that countries use to make sure people are treated fairly. It started a very long time ago in a place called Rome. Many countries like France and Germany use civil law. In civil law, there are books called codes that tell everyone what their rights and duties are. Judges look at these codes to decide what is right or wrong. This is different from common law, which is used in some other countries like England and the United States.
Qur'an\n\nThe Qur'an is the holy book of Islam. Muslims believe it is God's words. They think an angel named Gabriel told the words to a man named Muhammad a long time ago. The Qur'an is written in Arabic. Many Muslims read it in Arabic, but some read it in other languages to understand it better. The book has 114 parts called chapters. Each chapter has verses that tell people how to be good and kind. Muslims love and respect the Qur'an very much.
Pulse\n\nA pulse is a little thump you can feel in your body. It happens when your heart pushes blood through your veins. You can feel your pulse on your wrist, thumb, or neck. When you run and play, your pulse goes faster. A normal pulse is less than 100 thumps in one minute. If your pulse is too fast or too slow, you might be sick.
Graph\n\nA graph is a picture that shows how two things are connected. It has a line going up and a line going right. You can put dots on the graph to show numbers. For example, you can make a graph of how tall you are each year. The dots help you see if something is getting bigger or smaller. People use graphs to understand numbers better.
Osprey\n\nAn osprey is a big bird that eats fish. It is also called a fish hawk. It has dark brown wings, a white belly, and a white head with a dark stripe over its eyes. Its beak is black, and its feet are white with sharp black claws. The osprey has long, narrow wings and a short tail. When it flies, its wings make an arch shape. Ospreys live near water with lots of trees and lakes. In Scotland, people protect osprey nests so the birds can come back every year. Many people go to see them.
Lamprey\n\nA lamprey is a fish that looks like an eel and has no jaws. It has a round mouth like a sucking cup with sharp teeth. Lampreys live in rivers and oceans in cool parts of the world. They have no bones, only soft stuff like your ear. They have seven little holes on each side to breathe. Some lampreys are small like a ruler, and some are as long as a big dog.
Accent\n\nAn accent is the way a person says words. People from different places say the same words in a different way. For example, someone from Britain might sound different from someone from America. You can still understand them, but you can tell they are from another place. People learn to talk like the people around them when they are little. Even in the same country, people can have different accents. Long ago, accents were even stronger. Now, because of radio and TV, people sound more alike.
Knight\n\nA knight is a person who gets a special title from a king or queen. Long ago, knights were the best soldiers in the kingdom. They rode horses and wore heavy armor. They had a rule called chivalry, which meant they had to be brave and kind. Knights got land for their work. Today, knights do not fight anymore. King Charles III can still make someone a knight by tapping their shoulders with a sword. A knight is called "Sir" before their name. Some famous people like Bill Gates and Elton John have been made knights.
Gravel\n\nGravel is tiny pieces of rock that are loose on the ground. Some gravel pieces are as small as a grain of rice, and some are as big as a marble. Gravel is bigger than sand but smaller than big rocks. People use gravel to make roads and paths. They also mix gravel with sand and sticky stuff to make concrete for sidewalks and driveways. Gravel comes from old beaches that turned into rock a long time ago. Workers dig up the gravel and sort it by size. Most gravel is made of a hard material called silica. Sometimes people crush big rocks like granite to make gravel too.
Romania\n\nRomania is a country in Europe. It is near the Black Sea and the big Danube River. Tall mountains called the Carpathians go through the middle of Romania. The capital city is Bucharest, which is the biggest city. Many people live in Romania, about 19 million. The people there speak Romanian. Romania has four seasons: spring, summer, fall, and winter. In winter, snow falls on the mountains. The country has forests, rivers, and farms. Children go to school for ten years. Some famous foods from Romania are corn mush called mămăligă, sausages called mici, and stuffed cabbage rolls called sarmale. People celebrate Christmas and Easter, and also a special day called Great Union Day.
Narrative\n\nA narrative is a story. It tells about things that happen one after another. When you read a book or hear a tale, the narrative is the part that tells what happens. It is like the path the story follows from the beginning to the end.
Clothes dryer\n\nA clothes dryer is a machine that takes water out of wet clothes after washing. It has a round drum that spins the clothes around. Hot air blows into the drum to dry the clothes. The wet air goes out through a pipe. Some dryers use electricity to make heat. Others use gas. Some dryers do not have a pipe. They cool the air and collect the water in a tank or send it down a drain.
Scandinavian Mountains\n\nThe Scandinavian Mountains are a long chain of tall rocks that run through Norway, Sweden, and Finland. The mountains are very steep on the side that faces the sea, and they make deep, narrow water places called fjords. Some mountains are so high that snow and ice stay on them all year. The highest mountain in Norway is called Galdhpiggen. In Sweden, the highest is Kebnekaise. In Finland, the highest is Halti. These mountains are very cold because they are close to the Arctic. Many reindeer live there.
Table salt\n\nTable salt is a white mineral that people put on food to make it taste good. It comes from the sea or from rocks in the ground. When you mix salt with water, it disappears into the water. Salt helps your body work the right way, but eating too much can be bad for you. Long ago, people used salt to keep food from going bad.
Nice\n\nNice is a city in France, next to the sea. It has many beaches where you can play in the sand and swim in the water. The weather is warm and sunny in summer, and not too cold in winter. Many people visit Nice because it is beautiful. There are also museums with pretty paintings. The food in Nice is very good, like fish soup and salad. Some people there speak a different language called Nissart.
Slate\n\nSlate is a kind of rock that comes from mud and clay deep underground. It is pressed very hard and gets hot, which makes it split into flat, thin pieces. People use slate for roofs on houses to keep rain out. Some slate is used for floors, walls, and even gravestones. Long ago, children in school wrote on blackboards made of slate.
Airline\n\nAn airline is a company that flies people and things from one place to another in big airplanes. Some airlines have just one airplane, and some have many. Airlines take people to different cities and countries. They have to pay for fuel, pilots, and the people who help you get on the plane.
Mobile phone\n\nA mobile phone is a small phone that you can carry with you. It lets you talk to people far away without any wires. The phone uses radio waves to talk to a tall tower nearby, and the tower sends your voice to the other person. When you walk or drive, the phone switches from one tower to the next so your call keeps working. Many mobile phones today are smartphones. A smartphone is like a tiny computer. You can use it to send messages, take pictures, play games, and look at maps. Most smartphones have a touchscreen, which means you touch the screen to do things. People carry their mobile phones in their pockets or bags.
Sweden\n\nSweden is a country in the north of Europe, next to Norway and Finland. People who live there are called Swedes. The capital city is Stockholm, which is very big. Sweden has a king, but he does not make the rules. The people vote for who runs the country. Most people in Sweden speak Swedish. Sweden has not been in a war for a very long time. Many famous singers and sports players come from Sweden.
Aircraft\n\nAn aircraft is a machine that flies in the sky. Some aircraft have wings and move air over them to stay up, like airplanes, helicopters, and gliders. Other aircraft float in the sky, like balloons and airships. Most aircraft use an engine to fly, but gliders and balloons do not. Big airplanes that carry people are called airliners. They are the fastest way to travel and can fly over mountains and bad weather. The person who flies an aircraft is called a pilot.
Armadillo\n\nAn armadillo is a small animal with a hard shell on its back. The shell looks like armor and helps keep it safe. Armadillos live in warm places in South America and Central America. They like open areas like grasslands, but some live in forests too. Most armadillos are about as long as a big ruler, from their nose to the tip of their tail. The biggest kind, called the giant armadillo, can be as long as a yardstick and weigh as much as a big dog. A mother armadillo can have four babies at once, and all four babies look exactly the same because they come from one egg.
World's Fair\n\nA World's Fair is a big show where countries share their best things. People from all over the world come to see new machines, art, and food. The first World's Fair was a long time ago, in the 1800s. A group called the BIE helps make sure the fairs are fair and fun.
Concept\n\nA concept is an idea in your head. It is how you think about something. For example, the word "dog" is the name for the idea of a dog. Everything you know about a dog is the concept of a dog. Different words can mean the same idea. "Car" and "automobile" are different words for the same idea. People in different countries use different words for the same idea. That is how people can talk about the same thing in different languages.
Myanmar\n\nMyanmar is a country in Southeast Asia. It is very big and not an island. The capital city is Naypyidaw. The biggest city is Yangon. Myanmar has forests, rivers, and a long coast by the sea. It shares borders with China, Laos, Thailand, Bangladesh, and India. Many people live there. The country has many kinds of rocks and metals in the ground. A long time ago, a king ruled Myanmar. Then the British took over. Later, Japan took it for a while. Myanmar became its own country in 1948. After that, the army took charge and has been in charge for a long time. The army changed the name from Burma to Myanmar in 1989. Some people still call it Burma. The country has had many fights inside it for many years.
Barracuda\n\nA barracuda is a long fish that lives in warm oceans. It can grow as long as a big bed. Barracudas have sharp teeth and long bodies. They like to stay near the top of the water around sea grass and coral reefs. They eat fish that are silver and shiny. Sometimes they try to bite shiny things people wear, like bracelets, because they think it is a fish. But barracudas do not attack people very often. They swim very fast when they chase food.
Hades\n\nHades is a king in old Greek stories. He rules a place under the ground where people go after they die. Hades is the brother of Zeus and Poseidon. He is married to a goddess named Persephone. Hades has a special hat that makes him invisible. His favorite fruit is the pomegranate. People long ago were scared of Hades, so they did not build many temples for him.
Great Smoky Mountains National Park\n\nGreat Smoky Mountains National Park is a big park in the United States. It is in two states, Tennessee and North Carolina. The park has many tall mountains. Some mountains are so high that clouds sit on top of them. Many kinds of animals live there, like black bears, birds, and fish. There are also many trees and flowers. People can walk on trails and camp in the park. It is a very popular place to visit.
Atmospheric pressure\n\nAtmospheric pressure is the push of air all around us. The air is like a big blanket over the Earth. In some places the blanket is thicker, so the push is stronger. In other places the blanket is thinner, so the push is weaker. High up on a mountain, there is less air above, so the push is smaller. A tool called a barometer can measure this push. The push comes from every direction, not just from above.
Redwood\n\nA redwood is a very tall tree that grows in forests near the ocean in Northern California. It is one of the biggest trees in the world. Redwood trees have thick, hard bark that helps them stay safe from fire. Their cones open only after a fire. Some redwood trees are so big that many children could hold hands around them. The tallest tree in the world is a redwood named Hyperion. The biggest tree in the world by size is a redwood named General Sherman Tree.
White\n\nWhite is the brightest color. You can make white light by putting all the other colors together: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet. White is the color of snow and clouds. It makes us think of clean things, like a fresh sheet of paper. Many people wear white clothes for special happy days. Doctors and nurses wear white because it looks clean and safe.
Orion nebula\n\nThe Orion Nebula is a big, bright cloud in the night sky. You can see it with your eyes if you look near the belt of the Orion star picture. It is very far away, but it is the closest place where new stars are born. Inside the cloud, there are more than 700 baby stars that are just starting to grow. Some of these baby stars have flat, spinning disks around them. Those disks might one day turn into planets, just like the ones in our own sky. The Orion Nebula is like a big nursery for stars and planets.
Anglerfish\n\nAn anglerfish is a fish that lives deep in the ocean. It has a special part on its head that looks like a fishing pole with a little light at the end. The anglerfish uses the light to trick other fish into coming close. When the other fish swim near the light, the anglerfish opens its big mouth and eats them. Anglerfish are dark brown and have sharp teeth that point inward so their food cannot get away. Some anglerfish are very small, only as long as your finger. People in some parts of the world eat anglerfish as food.
Reflex\n\nA reflex is a very fast move your body makes all by itself. When something touches your hand, you pull it away before you even think. That is a reflex. Your body does this to keep you safe. The message to move does not go all the way to your brain. It goes to your spine and back to your muscle. That is why it is so fast. Even after a snake dies, its head can still bite. That is a reflex too.
Archaeopteryx\n\nArchaeopteryx is a very old animal that lived a long, long time ago, about 150 million years. It was a small dinosaur with feathers and wings, like a bird. But it also had a mouth with teeth, claws on its hands, and a long tail. Archaeopteryx could fly a little bit. Scientists found its bones in Germany. It helps us learn how some dinosaurs turned into birds.
Tigris\n\nThe Tigris is a very long river in the Middle East. It starts in the mountains in Turkey and flows through Syria and Iraq. The Tigris and another river called the Euphrates run close together. Long ago, people used the water from the Tigris to grow food for their families. The river is very important for the land around it.
French food\n\nFrench food is a kind of cooking that started in France. People all over the world like to eat it. French cooks use butter, cream, herbs, and cheese to make tasty dishes. They also make many kinds of sauces. Some famous French foods are quiche, which is like a pie with eggs and cheese, and bouillabaisse, which is a fish soup. In the north of France, people cook with butter. In the south, they use olive oil and garlic. French bread and cheese are very popular. Many people think French food is very special.
Naja\n\nA Naja is a kind of snake that can be very dangerous. It is called a true cobra. These snakes live in Africa and Asia. They can make the top part of their neck get big and flat. Some of them have pretty colors on their neck. They eat small animals like mice and birds. You should stay away from a Naja because it can hurt you.
Video game console\n\nA video game console is a machine that you use to play video games. It usually connects to a TV so you can see the game on the big screen. You hold a special controller in your hands to move the characters and play the game. Some consoles are small and you can carry them around. They have their own little screen, so you can play games anywhere. The Nintendo DS and PlayStation Portable are two kinds of handheld consoles. Some consoles can also run other programs, like Linux.
Cloud\n\nA cloud is made of tiny water drops or ice crystals high in the sky. Water from the ground goes up into the air and turns into a gas. When the air gets cold, the gas turns back into tiny drops that we see as clouds. Clouds can be white, gray, or even colorful at sunrise and sunset. Some clouds are big and fluffy, and some are thin and flat. When clouds get very full, the water drops fall down as rain or snow. Very big clouds can make thunder and lightning. Sometimes low clouds touch the ground, and we call that fog.
International Date Line\n\nThe International Date Line is an imaginary line that goes from north to south in the Pacific Ocean. It helps people know what day it is. When you cross this line going west, the date becomes one day later. When you cross it going east, the date becomes one day earlier. For example, if you fly from Tonga to Samoa, you might arrive the day before you left! The line is not straight. It bends around islands and countries so that all the islands in one country have the same date. Some places are on different sides of the line, so they have different days at the same time.
Sinai Peninsula\n\nThe Sinai Peninsula is a big piece of land in Egypt. It looks like a triangle. One side touches the Mediterranean Sea, and another side touches the Red Sea. It is the only part of Egypt that is in Asia. Many people live there. Long ago, different groups fought over this land. Now, people visit Sinai to see pretty coral reefs and Mount Sinai, a very special mountain.
Paris\n\nParis is a big city in France. It is the capital city, which means the most important city in the country. Many people live there. A river called the Seine runs through Paris. Paris has many old buildings and art museums. There is a train that goes underground called the Metro. People from all over the world visit Paris to see famous places like the Eiffel Tower. You can find food from many different countries there.
Sioux\n\nThe Sioux are a group of Native American people. They live in the middle part of the United States. Long ago, they met people who came from far away across the ocean. Today, the Sioux have two main groups called the Dakota and the Lakota. They speak different languages.
Ecuador\n\nEcuador is a small country in South America. It sits right on the equator, which is an imaginary line around the middle of the Earth. Ecuador has tall mountains called the Andes, thick jungles, and a coast on the Pacific Ocean. The capital city is Quito, which is high up in the mountains. The biggest city is Guayaquil on the coast. Ecuador also has the Galapagos Islands, which are far away in the ocean and have many special animals. People in Ecuador speak Spanish. The country grows bananas and cocoa, which is used to make chocolate. There are many old churches and buildings in Quito that are very beautiful.
Marriage\n\nMarriage is when two people promise to live together as a family. They often love each other and want to stay together for a long time. Some people get married in a church, and some get married in a special ceremony. Married people take care of each other and may have children. In some places, a man can be married to more than one woman. In other places, two men or two women can get married. People usually get married when they are grown-ups, between 25 and 30 years old.
So Tom and Prncipe\n\nSo Tom and Prncipe is a country made of two islands in the ocean near Africa. The islands are called So Tom and Prncipe. They are far apart from each other. The weather is hot and rainy. Many trees and plants grow there. People grow cocoa, which is used to make chocolate. The people speak Portuguese. The country used to belong to Portugal, but now it is its own country. The capital city is So Tom.
Monkey\n\nA monkey is an animal that lives in trees. Monkeys are smart and like to be with other monkeys. They have a tail, even if it is short. Some monkeys live in trees all the time, and some live on the ground too. Monkeys mostly eat fruit, but they also eat bugs and other food. They live in warm places like forests. Monkeys have long arms and legs to help them swing from tree to tree. Some monkeys can hold onto branches with their tails. The smallest monkey is the pygmy marmoset, which is very tiny. The biggest monkey is the mandrill, which is much bigger. A group of monkeys is called a troop.
Macau\n\nMacau is a small city in China, near the coast. It is a special place that makes its own rules, like having its own money and passport. Many people live there, more than half a million. Macau used to belong to Portugal, so some buildings and food have Portuguese style. People in Macau speak Cantonese most of the time. Macau is famous for its big casinos, where people play games for money. It makes a lot of money from gambling, even more than Las Vegas. Only in Macau can people gamble in China. Many rich people from China go there to play.
Impact event\n\nAn impact event is when two things in space crash into each other. This happens a lot in our Solar System. Most of the time, the things that crash are small, like rocks or ice balls. When a big rock hits a planet like Earth, it can make a big hole called a crater. You can see craters on the Moon and Mars. The air around Earth helps break up small rocks before they hit the ground. Sometimes we see them as bright streaks in the sky. A long time ago, a big rock hit Earth and helped make the Moon. Another big crash 66 million years ago may have made the dinosaurs go away. People watch the sky to see if any big rocks are coming toward Earth.
Kolkata\n\nKolkata is a big city in India. It is on the side of a river called the Hooghly. Many, many people live there. It was once the capital of India a long time ago. The city has old buildings and busy streets. People there speak a language called Bengali. Kolkata is also known as the "City of Joy." It has big markets, parks, and places to eat yummy food. Some people ride in yellow taxis or on trams that run on tracks. The city is very old, and people have lived there for a very long time.
Titan (mythology)\n\nThe Titans were big, strong beings from old Greek stories. They were the children of the Earth and the Sky. There were twelve of them, and they were the first gods to rule the world. Later, they fought a big war against the Olympian gods and lost. Some of the Titans were sent to a dark, deep place called Tartarus. The children of the Titans became other gods, like the Sun, the Moon, and the Dawn.
Neighbourhood\n\nA neighbourhood is a part of a city or town where people live close to each other. People in a neighbourhood often talk and help each other. Long ago, neighbourhoods helped keep people safe and clean. Some neighbourhoods have people who are from the same place or do the same job. Today, neighbourhoods can have groups that plan parties or watch out for each other.
Decapod\n\nA decapod is a sea animal with ten legs. Crabs, lobsters, shrimp, and crayfish are all decapods. They have a hard shell on the outside. The front two legs often have big claws for pinching. The other legs help them walk on the ocean floor. Some decapods eat dead plants and animals. Others eat small sea creatures or plants. They live in water all over the world.
History\n\nHistory is about things that happened a long time ago. People learn about history by looking at old things like books, letters, buildings, and tools. Museums keep these old things so we can see them. A person who studies history is called a historian. Sometimes people talk to old people who remember things from the past, and that is called oral history. Long ago, people in different parts of the world did not know about each other, so they each had their own history.
Messiah\n\nThe Messiah is a special person that some people believe God promised to send to help the world. In the Jewish religion, people think the Messiah will come to save them and make things better. In the Christian religion, people believe that Jesus is the Messiah. They say Jesus died and came back to life to help everyone. In the Muslim religion, people also believe Jesus is the Messiah and that he will come back one day. Different people have different ideas about what the Messiah will be like.
Radio broadcasting\n\nRadio broadcasting is when people send sounds through the air without wires. The sounds travel as waves from a tall tower to a radio in your home or car. You can hear music, news, and stories on the radio. Some radios use AM or FM to pick up the sounds. Other radios get signals from satellites high in the sky. Radio stations make their own shows or get them from other places.
Organ (biology)\n\nAn organ is a part inside your body that does a special job. Your heart is an organ that pumps blood. Your lungs are organs that help you breathe. Your stomach is an organ that helps break down food. All your organs work together to keep you healthy and strong.
Waste\n\nWaste is stuff that people do not want anymore. It is also called trash, garbage, or junk. Waste can be solid like old food, paper, or broken toys. It can also be liquid or gas. People throw away waste every day at home. Some waste, like fruit peels and paper, can be turned into new things. That is called recycling. Other waste is burned or buried in big piles called landfills. It is important to put waste in the right place so it does not hurt the earth or people.
Baby\n\nA baby is a very young person, younger than about 1 or 2 years old. A new baby is called a newborn. Babies cannot talk yet, so they cry to tell you what they need. A baby's head has soft spots that later turn into hard bone. Some babies are born with a funny-shaped head, but it gets round again soon. After a baby learns to walk, we call them a toddler.
Coral snake\n\nA coral snake is a small, colorful snake with red, yellow, white, and black bands. It has small fangs that shoot poison to catch its food. Coral snakes eat smaller snakes, lizards, frogs, baby birds, and mice. They are not mean and hardly ever bite people. Some coral snakes live in the United States, like in Florida and Texas. They like to live in dry, rocky places.
Bomber\n\nA bomber is a big airplane that drops bombs on the ground. Long ago, bombers had many people inside, like a pilot and gunners with machine guns. They flew low and slow. Today, bombers have only one or two people because computers help. They fly very fast and drop a bomb, then leave quickly.
Crab\n\nA crab is a small animal that lives in the sea. It has eight legs and two big claws called pincers. A crab uses its claws to catch food and to fight. Its body is hard like a shell. Crabs can be very tiny, like a pea, or very big, like a spider. They eat almost anything, like plants and small animals. People all over the world eat crabs for dinner. Some crabs live in the ocean, and some live on land.
Experience\n\nExperience is what you learn when you do something or watch someone else do it. It is learning by doing. For example, if you want to learn to play a game, you play it many times. You make mistakes and learn from them. That is better than just reading about the game. There are different kinds of experience. When you do or see something yourself, that is first-hand experience. When someone tells you about it, that is second-hand experience. When you imagine doing something and feel it in your mind, that is vicarious experience. Some people also have religious experiences, like dreams or visions where they feel close to God.
3D\n\n3D means something has three ways you can measure it. A box is 3D because it has length, width, and height. You can pick it up and turn it around to see all its sides. A piece of paper is not 3D because it is very thin. 3D pictures are used in video games and movies to make things look real. Your eyes help you see in 3D by looking from two different spots.
Nobility\n\nNobility is a group of people who were very important a long time ago. They were friends of the king or queen and helped rule the land. Nobles got land from the king and had to help him, especially by being soldiers. Many noble families passed their titles down to their children. Some nobles were very rich and did not have to work. Others were poor. Today, most countries do not give nobles special treatment, but in the United Kingdom, some nobles still have a seat in the House of Lords.
East Timor\n\nEast Timor is a small country in Southeast Asia. It is on an island called Timor, and it also has some smaller islands. The capital city is Dili, where many people live. East Timor has many mountains and is very hot. The country used to be ruled by Portugal, and then Indonesia took it over. In 2002, East Timor became its own country. People there speak Portuguese and other languages. The country is near Australia and Indonesia.
Saint Petersburg\n\nSaint Petersburg is a big city in Russia. It is near the sea and has a big port where ships come and go. Many people live there. A long time ago, a king named Peter the Great started the city. He wanted it to be a new kind of city with beautiful buildings and canals. Canals are like little rivers that people made. That is why some people call it the 'Venice of the North.' The city has changed its name a few times. During a big war, it was called Petrograd. Later it was called Leningrad. Now it is called Saint Petersburg again. There are pretty buildings like the Winter Palace and the Hermitage Museum. The city has many islands too.
Generation\n\nA generation is a group of people who were born around the same time. In a family, your brothers, sisters, and cousins are in the same generation as you. Your parents and their brothers and sisters are in a different generation. Grandparents are in another generation. Each generation is like a step on a family tree.
Vancouver\n\nVancouver is a big city in Canada, right next to the ocean. Many people live there, and they come from all over the world. The city has a big park called Stanley Park with beaches and tall wooden poles with carvings. There is also a mountain nearby where you can ski and see wolves and bears. Vancouver has sports teams that play hockey, football, and soccer. In 2010, the Winter Olympics were held there. The weather is usually not too hot or too cold, but it rains a lot.
African art\n\nAfrican art is art made by people who live in Africa. Africa is a very big place with many different countries. The art from each country can look different. Some African art is made of wood, clay, or metal. People carve shapes of animals and people. They also make colorful masks and cloth with bright patterns. Some art is used for dancing or special celebrations.
Human geography\n\nHuman geography is a kind of learning about people and the places where they live. It looks at how people and the world around them change each other. People live in different places, and they move from one place to another. They have different ways of doing things, like how they play and what they like. The way people live can change over time and in different spots on Earth. This kind of learning also looks at how people and their towns grow and change.
Sugar beet\n\nSugar beet is a plant that grows in the ground. Its big root is full of sweet stuff that people use to make sugar. Sugar beets are grown on farms so we can have sugar for our food. They are related to chard, which is a green vegetable you can eat. Many countries grow sugar beets, and about one-third of all the sugar in the world comes from them.
Solar eclipse\n\nA solar eclipse happens when the moon moves right between the earth and the sun. The moon blocks the sun's light for a little while. This can only happen when the moon is new. During a total solar eclipse, the sky gets dark in the middle of the day. It looks like night for a few minutes. Long ago, people thought a solar eclipse was a bad sign. Today, people know it is just a natural event. You should never look directly at the sun during an eclipse because it can hurt your eyes very badly. Special glasses can keep your eyes safe.
Data\n\nData is a bunch of facts and numbers that people collect. It helps grown-ups make good choices. For example, if you count how many toys you have, that is data. Computers store data as tiny bits inside them. Data can be things you can see, like colors, or things you can count, like how many cookies are in a jar. When you put data together, you can learn something new, like how warm it is outside.
Hangul\n\nHangul is the alphabet used for writing the Korean language. A long time ago, a king named Sejong made Hangul in 1443. He wanted people to be able to read and write easily. The letters in Hangul look like the shapes your mouth makes when you say them. That is why Hangul is easy to learn. Today, people in North Korea and South Korea use Hangul to write. When you write Hangul, you put letters together in little blocks. Each block makes one sound, like 'han' or 'geul'.
Dnieper\n\nThe Dnieper is a very long river in Europe. It starts in Russia, goes through Belarus and Ukraine, and ends in the Black Sea. It is one of the biggest rivers in Europe. Long ago, Greek people called it the Borysthenes.
Biome\n\nA biome is a big area on Earth where certain plants and animals live. For example, a hot and dry place is a desert biome, and a cold and snowy place is a tundra biome. Different biomes have different weather and different kinds of trees and animals. Some biomes are forests, grasslands, or deserts. The plants and animals in a biome are good at living in that place.
Ice age\n\nAn ice age is a very long time when the Earth is very cold. The cold makes big sheets of ice grow on the land and at the North and South Poles. During an ice age, the ocean gets lower because a lot of water is frozen into ice. Sometimes it gets a little warmer for a short time, and then it gets cold again. The last cold time ended about 11,000 years ago. Now we are in a warm time. Big ice sheets still cover Greenland and Antarctica. People have been burning things that make the Earth warmer, so the ice is melting.
Yosemite National Park\n\nYosemite National Park is a big park in California, USA. It has tall waterfalls, like Yosemite Falls, which is one of the tallest in the world. Many people visit every year to see the beautiful valley and big rocks. Most of the park is wild nature with trees and animals.
Earth science\n\nEarth science is about our planet Earth. It is the study of what Earth is made of, how it works, and how it changes. Earth science has many parts. Geology is about rocks, mountains, and volcanoes. Oceanography is about the big oceans that cover most of Earth. Meteorology is about the sky and weather, like rain and wind. Astronomy looks at how the Sun and Moon affect Earth. All these parts work together to help us understand Earth better.
Bathing\n\nBathing is when you put your body in water to get clean. People take baths in a bathtub or shower to wash away dirt and feel fresh. Sometimes people bathe just for fun, like splashing in a pool. Bathing can also help you feel better when you are sick. Some people even bathe in mud or chocolate, but most of the time we use water and soap.
Vampire bat\n\nA vampire bat is a kind of bat that drinks blood. Most bats eat bugs or fruit, but vampire bats drink blood from other animals. They live in warm places like Mexico, Brazil, Chile, and Argentina. Vampire bats sleep in big groups of up to 100 bats. They can spread sickness, so people stay away from them. Their spit has a special thing that stops blood from getting thick, and doctors use that to help people with heart problems. Some bats look like vampire bats but eat fruit or small animals instead of blood.
Ultrasound\n\nUltrasound is a sound that is too high for people to hear. Some animals like dogs, bats, and dolphins can hear it. Doctors use ultrasound to take pictures of babies inside their mommies. It is safe because it does not use x-rays. Ultrasound can also clean things like glasses and jewelry by making tiny bubbles that pop and wash away dirt.
Feminism\n\nFeminism is about making sure boys and girls are treated the same and have the same rights. A long time ago, women could not vote or do many things that men could do. Some brave women called suffragettes held big protests so women could vote. Later, feminism worked for other things like jobs, school, and how women are treated at home. Today, feminism still helps make the world fair for everyone, no matter if you are a boy or a girl.
Miracle\n\nA miracle is something very special and amazing that happens. It is so wonderful that people think it must be a gift from God or another powerful being. Some miracles are big, like when the moon was split into two pieces. Other miracles are small and happen to just one person. Many people believe in miracles, and they read about them in books like the Bible.
Bark\n\nBark is the outside covering of a tree. It is like a coat that keeps the tree safe. Some bark is rough and bumpy, and some bark is smooth. Bark can be brown, gray, or even white. It grows on the trunk and branches of the tree. Bark helps the tree stay strong and healthy.
Bone\n\nBones are the hard parts inside your body that make up your skeleton. They hold your body up and help you move. Without bones, you would be like a soft pile on the ground. Bones also protect important parts inside you. Your skull protects your brain, and your ribs protect your heart and lungs. Bones are alive and need exercise and food like milk and spinach to stay strong. The soft part inside some bones, called bone marrow, makes your blood cells.
Money\n\nMoney is what people use to buy things they need or want. A long time ago, people did not use money. They traded things like cows or wheat for other things. But that was hard because cows are big and wheat can go bad. So people started using coins made of metal. The first coins were made in a place called Lydia a very long time ago. Later, people used paper money too. Today, money can also be numbers in a bank computer. Different countries have different kinds of money, like dollars or rials. Money helps us get food, toys, and clothes.
Saffron\n\nSaffron is a spice that comes from a flower. It is very expensive. People use it to give food a yellow color and a special taste. Saffron tastes a little bitter and smells like hay. It comes from a purple flower that grows in the fall. The flower has three red parts inside that are picked by hand. It takes many flowers to make just a little bit of saffron. People have used saffron for a very long time, even thousands of years ago. They put it in food, tea, and baths.
Hedgehog\n\nA hedgehog is a small animal with many sharp spines on its back. It has between 5000 and 7000 spines. Hedgehogs live in Europe, Asia, Africa, and New Zealand. When they are scared, they curl up into a ball. They eat bugs, snails, frogs, snakes, bird eggs, mushrooms, berries, and melons. Sometimes they look for worms after rain. Hedgehogs sleep during the day and wake up at night. They sleep a lot in the winter, from November to March. Their spines are not poisonous and are safe to touch. Some people keep hedgehogs as pets, but they are not allowed in some places.
Okra\n\nOkra is a green vegetable that grows on a plant. It is also called lady's fingers. The plant has flowers and is related to cotton and hibiscus. People eat the green seed pods when they are still small and soft. Okra can be fried, grilled, or put in soup. It is a popular vegetable in many warm countries like Nigeria, Ghana, India, and Pakistan.
Dock\n\nA dock is a flat place built over water where boats can park. It is like a wooden floor that sticks out from the land into the water. People tie their boats to the dock so the boats do not float away. The dock is held up by long poles that go deep into the ground under the water.
Colonization\n\nColonization is when people from one country move to another place to live and take control of it. A long time ago, people from Europe went to North America and South America. They built new towns and farms there. Many of the people who already lived there were hurt or killed. Today, most people in North America have families that came from Europe long ago. Some stories about space talk about people living on other planets, which would be a new kind of colonization.
Antelope\n\nAn antelope is an animal that lives in Africa and parts of Asia. It has four legs with hooves and eats grass. Antelopes have horns on their heads that never fall off. Some antelopes are very fast and can jump high. A group of antelopes is called a herd. Many antelopes move to new places when it rains to find fresh grass to eat.
Evolution\n\nEvolution is how living things change over a very long time. It is how new kinds of animals and plants come to be. All living things are a little bit different from each other. Some differences help them find food, stay safe, or have babies. These good differences get passed to their babies. Over many, many years, living things change so much that they become new kinds of animals or plants. We know this happened because we find old bones and shells in rocks, called fossils. Fossils show that animals and plants from long ago are not the same as the ones today. Scientists also look at the tiny parts inside living things, called DNA, to see how they are related. All life on Earth comes from one very old living thing.
United Nations\n\nThe United Nations is a group of many countries that work together. It started in 1945 after a big war to help countries talk instead of fight. Almost every country in the world is part of it. The main home of the United Nations is in New York City. People from different countries meet there to make rules and help each other. The United Nations also sends helpers to places where there is trouble to keep peace. It works to stop people from being hungry or sick and to take care of the Earth.
Meal\n\nA meal is food that people eat. People usually eat three meals each day. The first meal is breakfast, which you eat in the morning. Breakfast can have cereal, bread, fruit, and milk. The next meal is lunch, which you eat around noon. Lunch can be a sandwich, soup, or fruit. The last meal is dinner, which you eat in the evening. Dinner often has meat, rice or pasta, vegetables, and sometimes a sweet treat like cake.
Table (furniture)\n\nA table is a piece of furniture with a flat top and legs that hold it up. People put things on a table, like food, cups, books, or toys. Some tables have a cloth on top. You can make some tables bigger by pulling the top out. Some tables fold up so you can carry them, like for camping. There are small tables on trains and planes that fold down. A round table might have a Lazy Susan that spins in the middle. A table used outside is called a picnic table. In Japan, some tables are low and round for tea and food.
Mile\n\nA mile is a way to measure how far something is. It is like a long line on the ground. People in the United States and the United Kingdom use miles to say how far they have walked or driven. A long time ago, the Romans made up the mile. They said it was one thousand steps. Today, a mile is a little longer than one and a half kilometers. There is also a special mile for boats and airplanes called a nautical mile. When a boat goes one nautical mile in one hour, we say it is going one knot.
Plaice\n\nA plaice is a fish that lives in the sea. It is flat and has both eyes on one side of its head. The top side of a plaice is brown with orange spots, and the bottom side is white. Plaice likes to hide on the sandy bottom of the ocean.
Fruit\n\nA fruit is a part of a plant that holds seeds. Many fruits are sweet and good to eat. Fruits grow on trees, bushes, or vines. Some fruits have a soft inside and a thin skin, like grapes and blueberries. Other fruits have a hard skin, like pumpkins and watermelons. Apples and pears have a core in the middle that you do not eat. Peaches and olives have a hard pit inside. Fruits have water and sugar, which makes them taste yummy. Animals and people eat fruits, and the seeds inside help new plants grow.
Gibbon\n\nA gibbon is a small ape that lives in warm forests in places like Sumatra, Thailand, and Malaysia. Gibbons are very good at swinging from tree to tree using their long arms. They can also walk on the ground with their arms up in the air. Gibbons make loud singing sounds that travel far through the forest. They sing to talk to other gibbons and to tell strangers to stay away. During the day, gibbons look for leaves, flowers, fruit, and bugs to eat. At night, they sleep in trees. Male gibbons are usually black, and female gibbons are often light yellow. A baby gibbon is called an offspring, and gibbons can live for about 25 years.
Arctic Circle\n\nThe Arctic Circle is an imaginary line around the top part of the Earth. It is very cold there. Inside the Arctic Circle, the sun does not come up in the middle of winter, and it does not go down in the middle of summer. The North Pole is in the middle of the Arctic Circle. Some countries like Canada, Russia, and Norway are partly inside the Arctic Circle.
Pufferfish\n\nA pufferfish is a fish that can puff up like a ball. When it feels scared, it gulps water and gets twice as big. Then it swims very slowly. Most pufferfish live in warm ocean water near coral reefs. Some live in rivers too. They have four big teeth that are stuck together like a plate. They use these teeth to crunch hard shells of crabs and snails. Pufferfish are very poisonous, so you should never eat one unless a special chef makes it safe. In Japan, people eat a special kind called fugu. Some people keep pufferfish as pets in fish tanks.
Dentistry\n\nDentistry is a job about teeth. A dentist is a doctor who checks teeth, fixes them, and helps stop tooth problems. Some helpers work with the dentist. A dental hygienist helps people clean their teeth. A dental assistant helps the dentist when fixing a patient's teeth. A dental surgeon fixes big tooth problems with surgery. An orthodontist moves teeth with braces.
Rule of law\n\nThe rule of law means that everyone must follow the same rules, even the people in charge of the country. No one is allowed to break the law just because they are powerful. The rule of law helps keep people safe and stops anyone from being a dictator. It also makes sure that the government uses money fairly. Many countries use the rule of law to protect the rights of all people.
Espionage\n\nEspionage is when someone tries to find out secret information without asking. This is also called spying. A spy is a person who looks for secrets about a group or a country. Sometimes a spy works for two sides at once. Spying is against the rules in a war.
Quarry\n\nA quarry is a big hole in the ground where people dig up rocks. Workers cut the rocks into big blocks to build houses and other buildings. When a quarry is done being used, it can fill up with water and become a little lake.
Volume\n\nVolume is how much space something takes up. A big rock takes up more space than a little rock. Everything around you takes up space, even a thin piece of paper. People measure volume with special tools. For liquids, you can pour them into a cup with marks on the side. For a small toy, you can put it in water and see how much the water goes up. Volume can change if you squeeze something soft, like a sponge.
Scotland\n\nScotland is a country that is part of the United Kingdom. It is in the north part of the island of Great Britain. The capital city is Edinburgh. The biggest city is Glasgow. About five million people live there. Scotland has many islands and a long coast. The North Sea is to the east and the Atlantic Ocean is to the west. Long ago, Scotland was its own kingdom. Now it is part of the United Kingdom. People in Scotland speak English and some speak Scottish Gaelic.
Soldier\n\nA soldier is a person who works in an army. Some soldiers choose to join, and some are asked to join. There are many kinds of soldiers. Some drive tanks, some jump from planes, and some help sick people. Soldiers wear special clothes and follow orders to keep their country safe.
Addis Ababa\n\nAddis Ababa is a big city in Africa. It is the capital of a country called Ethiopia. Many people from different places live there. They speak many different languages. The city is high up on a mountain. It was started a long time ago by a king and queen. There is a big school there called a university. Many people live in Addis Ababa today.
Free will\n\nFree will is being able to choose between different actions. It means you can decide what to do, like picking a toy or a snack. If you could not choose, then saying something is good or bad would not make sense. People give advice and make rules because they think you can choose. In court, judges and juries try to find out if someone decided to do something bad on purpose. Some people think the world works like a clock, where everything is already decided. That idea is called determinism. If that were true, then free will would not exist. But many people believe we do have free will, because we feel like we make choices every day.
Ninja\n\nA ninja was a kind of spy who lived in Japan a long time ago. Ninjas were very good at hiding and sneaking. They wore dark blue, red, or brown clothes, not always black. Ninjas could pretend to be other people, like a merchant or a traveling monk. They used short swords and other weapons. Ninjas were trained from a young age to be strong and smart. They could climb walls and move quietly. Some people thought ninjas could fly, but that is just a story. Today, you see ninjas in movies and cartoons.
Humpback whale\n\nA humpback whale is a very big animal that lives in the ocean. It has long front flippers and a bumpy head. Humpback whales can be found in every ocean. They can grow as long as a big bus and weigh as much as many cars. They eat tiny shrimp and small fish. Sometimes they blow bubbles in a circle to trap their food. Male humpback whales sing long songs that can last many hours. They make sounds by pushing air through their nose. We do not know why they sing. Both males and females make grunts and moans to talk to each other. Humpback whales live alone and travel far each year.
Labrador Sea\n\nThe Labrador Sea is a big part of the ocean near Canada and Greenland. It is very deep in some places and gets shallower near the north. In winter, much of the sea is covered with ice. Seals have their babies on the ice in early spring. Many fish live there, like salmon and cod. People used to catch a lot of cod, but then there were not enough fish, so they stopped. Whales also swim in the sea, like sei whales and minke whales. Birds like ducks and geese live near the coast. Plants like black spruce and Labrador tea grow along the shore. People make tea from Labrador tea leaves.
Taekwondo\n\nTaekwondo is a way of fighting that started in Korea. It uses your hands and feet to kick and punch. Kicking is very important in taekwondo because your legs are strong and long. People practice taekwondo to get strong, fast, and balanced. You can also learn to break a board with your hand or foot. In taekwondo, you wear a belt that shows how much you have learned. The belt colors start with white and go to black. Respect is a big part of taekwondo. You bow to your teacher and to other students. Taekwondo is a sport in the Olympic Games.
Sun\n\nThe Sun is a big, hot ball of gas in the sky. It is a star, just like the stars you see at night, but much closer to us. The Sun gives us light and heat. Without the Sun, Earth would be too cold for anything to live. Plants need sunlight to grow, and animals and people need plants to eat and breathe. The Sun is very, very big. More than one million Earths could fit inside it. The Sun is made mostly of two kinds of gas: hydrogen and helium. Deep inside the Sun, hydrogen turns into helium and makes a lot of energy. This energy travels to Earth as light and heat. It takes about eight minutes for sunlight to reach us. The Sun looks yellow from Earth, but it is really white. Sometimes you can see dark spots on the Sun called sunspots. The Sun is about four and a half billion years old. It will keep shining for a very long time.
Aegean Sea\n\nThe Aegean Sea is a big body of water between Greece and Turkey. It is part of the Mediterranean Sea. Many islands are in this sea, like Crete and Rhodes. Long ago, people called the Minoans and Mycenaeans lived near the Aegean Sea. They sailed on boats to trade with each other. Some of the islands have mountains that go underwater. Other islands have safe places for boats to stop. A few islands have volcanoes, and some have rocks that people use to make things. The sea is blue and pretty, and many people visit it.
Climate\n\nClimate is what the weather is usually like in a place over a very long time, like thirty years. Weather is what happens outside today, but climate is the big picture. There are different kinds of climate: hot and wet like a jungle, hot and dry like a desert, warm and cool like where you live, cold like the North Pole, and warm with dry summers like near the sea. Where you live on Earth, how high the ground is, and if there is a big ocean nearby can change the climate. People can make the climate warmer in some places, but sometimes places get very cold too.
Jade\n\nJade is a pretty stone that comes in many colors. People use it to make jewelry like necklaces and rings. Long ago, people in China and the Maori used jade to make knives and tools because it is very hard. Later, people liked jade because it looked nice and they thought it was lucky. Only rich people could have jade because it was rare and cost a lot of money.
Ancient Egypt\n\nAncient Egypt was a very old country that started a long, long time ago. It grew along the Nile River, which gave water for growing food. The people there built big stone buildings called temples and tombs. They had a special way of writing with pictures called hieroglyphs. The rulers were called pharaohs, and people thought they were close to the gods. The Egyptians believed in many gods and goddesses, like Ra the sun god and Bastet the cat goddess. They also made mummies of dead people and cats. Farming was important because the Nile flooded every year and left rich dirt for growing wheat and barley. The people paid taxes with food or work instead of money.
Riyadh\n\nRiyadh is a big city in Saudi Arabia. It is the capital, which means it is the most important city in the country. Many people live there, more than six million. Riyadh is in the middle of a hot desert, so summers are very hot. In winter, it is warm but the nights can be cool. There is not much rain, but sometimes dust storms blow sand everywhere. The city has old places like Diriyah, which is a special old town that people visit. There are tall buildings like the Kingdom Center. People in Riyadh go shopping, eat food, and have fun.
Time zone\n\nA time zone is a part of the world where everyone uses the same clock time. The Earth is round, so when it is daytime on one side, it is nighttime on the other side. There are 24 time zones. Each time zone has a name, like the Eastern Time Zone in North America. Long ago, each city had its own time. Then trains started going fast between cities, so people made time zones to help everyone know what time it is. The main time zone is called UTC. Some places change their clocks in summer to have more daylight in the evening. That is called Daylight Saving Time.
Smelting\n\nSmelting is a way to get metal from rocks called ore. Most metals like iron, copper, and silver are found mixed with other stuff in the ground. To get the metal out, people heat the ore very hot in a special oven. Sometimes they add other things to help clean the metal. The hot metal melts and flows out, and the leftover rock turns into slag. Slag can be used to make bricks or roads. Iron is made in a tall oven called a blast furnace. Copper is heated on a fire to burn off bad stuff. Aluminum needs electricity to be made from its ore. Smelting helped people long ago make tools and build things.
Cyclone\n\nA cyclone is a big, spinning wind that goes around and around. It is like a giant circle of wind in the sky. The wind blows very fast and can knock down trees and houses. Cyclones have a quiet spot in the middle called the eye. Around the eye, the wind blows the hardest. Cyclones are also called hurricanes or typhoons in different places. They can be very dangerous, so people must stay inside when one comes.
Family name\n\nA family name is a name that people in the same family share. In English, it is called a last name or surname, and it comes at the end of a person's full name. Children usually have the same family name as their father. When a woman gets married, she often changes her last name to be the same as her husband's. For example, if Mary Brown marries John Smith, she becomes Mary Smith, and their children are David Smith and Kate Smith. Sometimes people use their mother's family name instead. In some languages, the family name comes first. In Spanish, children get both parents' family names. In Russian, the family name changes if the person is a boy or a girl. Some people, like the Javanese, do not use family names at all.
Printmaking\n\nPrintmaking is a way to make art by printing pictures, usually on paper. The good thing about printmaking is that you can make many copies of the same picture. Each copy is called a print. The artist makes a picture on a flat piece of wood, metal, or stone. Then they put ink on it and press paper on top. The picture shows up on the paper. You can do this many times to make lots of prints. Some prints are made with wood blocks, and some are made with linoleum. People have been making prints for a very long time.
