Then it becomes a tiny swimming baby called a tadpole. After a while, it grows legs and leaves the water for a year. This young newt is called an eft. When it grows up, it goes back to the water to have babies. Some newts stay in the water all the time. Others live on land but go to the water each year to lay eggs. Newts have bright colors to warn other animals that they taste bad. Their skin makes a poison that can hurt animals that try to eat them. You can touch a newt, but you must wash your hands after because the poison can make you sick.
Abdomen\n\nThe abdomen is the part of your body between your chest and your legs. It holds your tummy and other parts inside that help you eat and go to the bathroom. The muscles in your abdomen help you bend and sit up.
Beard\n\nA beard is the hair that grows on the bottom part of a man's face. Some men have a lot of beard hair, and some have only a little. The hair above the mouth is called a mustache. Many men cut or shave their beard to keep it short. Some animals have hair that looks like a beard too.
Vowel\n\nA vowel is a sound you make with your mouth open. In English, the letters A, E, I, O, and U are called vowels. Every word has a vowel in it. The letter Y can sometimes be a vowel, like in the word 'sky'. The letter W can also be part of a vowel sound, like in 'cow'. Vowels help us say words.
War elephant\n\nA war elephant is a big, strong elephant that people taught to help in a fight. Long ago, soldiers would ride on the elephant and guide it toward the enemy. The elephant would run fast, knock down people, and break their lines. War elephants were first used in a faraway country called India. Later, other countries used them too. A famous man named Hannibal took elephants across big snowy mountains to fight. But then people made loud boom sticks called cannons, and elephants were not used for fighting anymore. After that, elephants helped with heavy work like moving big logs.
Callisto (moon)\n\nCallisto is a big round moon that goes around the planet Jupiter. It is almost as big as the planet Mercury. Callisto was found a long time ago by a man named Galileo. One side of Callisto always faces Jupiter, and the other side never sees it. The moon is made of rock and ice, and it has many holes called craters on its surface. There might be a big ocean of water under the ice. Callisto has a very thin air around it. Some people think we might be able to live there one day.
Mountain\n\nA mountain is a very big and tall part of the ground that goes up high into the sky. Mountains are bigger and steeper than hills. The top of a mountain is called the summit or peak. Some mountains are made when big pieces of the ground push together and fold up like a rug. Other mountains are made when the ground cracks and one side lifts up. Some mountains are made when hot melted rock comes out of the ground and piles up. The highest mountain on Earth is Mount Everest. Mountains can be found all over the world, and they are home to many animals and plants.
Banff National Park\n\nBanff National Park is a very big park in Canada. It was the first national park in Canada, made a long time ago in 1885. The park has tall mountains, big fields of ice, and lots of green trees. There is a town called Banff near the park. Many people go there to see the mountains and play outside.
Kangaroo\n\nA kangaroo is an animal that lives in Australia. It hops to move around fast. Kangaroos have strong back legs and a long tail. They can hop very far, about three times their own height. They can also swim. Kangaroos eat grass and plants. A mother kangaroo carries her baby, called a joey, in a pouch on her belly. Kangaroos live in groups called mobs. They are a symbol of Australia. Kangaroos can be dangerous because they kick with their strong legs.
Kumquat\n\nA kumquat is a tiny fruit that looks like a small orange. It grows on a small tree with shiny green leaves and white flowers. The tree can have small thorns. You can eat the whole kumquat, even the skin. The inside is a little sour, and the skin is sweet. Kumquats come from China and Japan. They are very tough and can grow in cold places where other oranges cannot.
Computer\n\nA computer is a machine that works with information. It can take in information, change it, save it, and show it. You can tell a computer what to do by using a keyboard, a mouse, or a touch screen. Computers can do many things very fast, like play games, show videos, and help you write. Some computers are small, like phones and laptops. Some are big and help run traffic lights or washing machines. Computers follow instructions called programs. People who write these instructions are called programmers. A long time ago, a man named Charles Babbage thought of the first computer, but he never built it. Today, many people have a computer at home or at work.
Rugby union\n\nRugby union is a sport where two teams of 15 players try to score points with an oval ball. The field is a big rectangle with H-shaped goal posts at each end. Players can score a try by putting the ball down behind the goal posts, which gives 5 points. After a try, they can kick the ball through the goal posts for 2 more points. They can also kick for 3 points during play or from a penalty. The game lasts 80 minutes, and the team with the most points wins. Players must pass the ball sideways or backwards, not forward. Only the player with the ball can be tackled. There is a referee who makes sure everyone follows the rules.
Grandparent\n\nA grandparent is the parent of your mom or dad. A boy grandparent is called a grandfather, and a girl grandparent is called a grandmother. Grandparents often have more time to play and have fun with their grandchildren than parents do. Some people call their grandparents 'grandma,' 'grandpa,' 'granny,' or 'nana.' A grandchild is the child of a grandparent's son or daughter. A boy grandchild is a grandson, and a girl grandchild is a granddaughter. Great-grandparents are the parents of your grandparents. Many children today get to know their great-grandparents because people live longer now.
Basket weaving\n\nBasket weaving is a way to make things by weaving or sewing materials together. People who do this are called basket makers. They can make baskets, mats, bags, or even furniture. You take long pieces of grass, leaves, or thin sticks and cross them over and under each other to make a shape.
Subtraction\n\nSubtraction is taking away some things from a group. If you have seven cookies and you eat four, you have three left. We write that as 7 minus 4 equals 3. The minus sign means take away. Subtraction helps you find out how many are left. When you buy something and pay with more money, the store uses subtraction to give you the right change.
Broccoli\n\nBroccoli is a green vegetable that looks like a little tree. It has a thick stalk and a green top made of many tiny flower buds. Broccoli comes from Italy and is now eaten by people all over the world. It is good for you because it has vitamins that help your body stay strong. You can eat it raw or cooked. Some people like to dip it in ranch dressing. When broccoli grows too long, it turns into yellow flowers.
Eid al-Adha\n\nEid al-Adha is a special holiday for Muslims all around the world. On this day, people remember a story from long ago about a man named Ibrahim who loved God very much. God asked Ibrahim to give up his son, but at the last moment God sent a lamb instead. So on Eid al-Adha, Muslims share meat from a sheep, goat, or cow with their family and with people who do not have much food. They also pray together, give gifts to children, and have a big feast. It is a happy time to show love for God and help others.
Computer security\n\nComputer security is about keeping computers safe. It tells computers what not to do, so bad people cannot break them. People use passwords and locks to protect their computers. This keeps your games, pictures, and information safe from others.
British Museum\n\nThe British Museum is a big building in London where old things from all over the world are kept. It opened a long time ago, in 1759, and was the first museum that let everyone come in for free. The museum has millions of objects, like the Rosetta Stone, which helped people understand old Egyptian writing. It also has the Elgin Marbles, which are stone carvings from Greece. The museum has a huge room with a big glass roof called the Great Court. Many people visit every year to see the old statues, pots, and treasures from Egypt, Greece, Rome, and other places.
Nail\n\nA nail is a small piece of metal. It has a flat top and a pointy end. People use a hammer to push the nail into wood or other things. Nails help hold two pieces of wood together. You can see nails in walls, furniture, and toys. They are very old and were used by people long ago.
Computer mouse\n\nA computer mouse is a small thing you hold in your hand to use a computer. You move it on a flat table or a mouse pad, and a little arrow on the screen moves too. When you push the left button, you can click on pictures or words to open them. The right button opens a special menu. Between the two buttons there is a little wheel that you can roll to make the screen go up or down. Some mice have no wire and use batteries to talk to the computer. Many computers have a mouse, but laptops also have a flat trackpad that does the same thing.
Nepali language\n\nThe Nepali language is a way of talking and writing that people use in Nepal and some parts of India. It is the main language of Nepal, and the government uses it for all official work. Many people in Nepal speak Nepali as their first language. It is written with special letters that look like the letters used for Hindi. Kids in Nepal have to learn Nepali in school until they finish tenth grade.
Plane (tool)\n\nA plane is a tool that people use to make wood flat and smooth. It has a sharp metal blade inside a block of wood or metal. When you push the plane across a piece of wood, it shaves off thin slices and makes the surface even. People have used planes for thousands of years to build furniture and other things.
Dominica\n\nDominica is a small island in the Caribbean Sea. It is a country where people speak English. The island has lots of green rainforests and a big hot spring called Boiling Lake. The capital city is Roseau. About 70,000 people live there. The island is sometimes called the 'Nature Island of the Caribbean' because it has so many beautiful plants and animals. People on Dominica like to play cricket, which is a game with a bat and ball.
Velocity\n\nVelocity is how fast something moves and which way it goes. Speed tells how fast, but velocity tells the direction too. If a car goes 10 miles per hour to the east, that is its velocity. To find average velocity, you see how far something moved and how long it took. Instantaneous velocity is how fast something is going at one exact moment. You can also compare two things moving to find relative velocity.
Rabbi\n\nA rabbi is a teacher in the Jewish religion. Rabbis learn a lot about Jewish rules and stories. They teach people about the Torah, which is a special book. Rabbis also help lead prayers and celebrations in the Jewish community. Some rabbis help make sure food is prepared in a special way called kosher. Long ago, only men could be rabbis. Today, many women are rabbis too. Three rabbis can work together to help solve problems between people.
Ursa Minor\n\nUrsa Minor is a group of stars in the sky. It is also called the Little Bear or the Little Dipper. The stars look like a cup with a long handle. The star at the end of the handle is the North Star, which is also called Polaris. The North Star helps people know which way is north. Ursa Minor has seven bright stars that make the shape of a dipper. The Little Dipper is smaller than the Big Dipper. In old stories, people said the Little Bear had a long tail because a baby bear was spun around the sky by its tail.
Extrasolar planet\n\nAn extrasolar planet is a planet that goes around a star far, far away from our own Sun. Our solar system has eight planets, but there are many other planets in space. Some of these planets are big like Jupiter, and some are small like Earth. A few might even have water, just like our planet. Scientists find these planets by looking at stars that get a little darker when a planet passes in front of them. The nearest star with planets is Alpha Centauri, but it is too far to visit. There are billions of extrasolar planets in our galaxy.
Australia\n\nAustralia is a big country that is also an island. It is in the southern part of the world. The capital city is Canberra, and the biggest city is Sydney. Australia is mostly hot and dry, with a big desert in the middle. About 27 million people live there, and most of them live near the east coast. Australia has special animals that do not live anywhere else, like kangaroos, koalas, and platypuses. The first people to live there were called Aboriginal Australians and Torres Strait Islanders. They arrived a very long time ago, more than 50,000 years ago. Australia is known for mining things like coal and gold, and for making wool. The national flower is the golden wattle.
Amber\n\nAmber is a hard, yellow-orange stone that comes from old tree resin. Resin is a sticky liquid that oozes out of some trees. Long, long ago, the resin got hard and turned into amber. Sometimes tiny bugs, spiders, or leaves got stuck in the sticky resin and are still inside the amber today. People use amber to make pretty beads, jewelry, and other decorations. Most amber in the world comes from a place near the Baltic Sea in Russia. Amber can be many colors, like yellow, orange, brown, and even green or blue. It feels smooth and warm to touch.
Ball\n\nA ball is a round thing you can play with. It can be big like a basketball or small like a marble. Some balls are hollow and some are solid. You can throw a ball, catch it, or kick it. People play games with balls, like baseball and basketball. Animals like armadillos can curl up into a ball shape. You can also make a fist into a ball.
Life\n\nLife is something that can make more of itself. It is different from things that are not alive. All life on Earth needs water and uses the sun for energy. Living things grow, change, and make babies. They can be very small, like a tiny cell, or very big, like a tree or a whale. There are many kinds of life on Earth, such as plants, animals, and tiny things you can only see with a special tool. Life is all around us, in the ground, in the water, and in the air.
Manta ray\n\nA manta ray is a very big fish that lives in warm ocean water near coral reefs. It is the biggest kind of ray. A manta ray can be very wide and very heavy. It has a big brain for its body size. Manta rays swim deep in the cold ocean. Some manta rays travel far, and some stay near reefs. Big sharks like tiger sharks may try to eat manta rays.
Negative number\n\nA negative number is a number that is smaller than zero. You write it with a minus sign in front, like -3. On a number line, negative numbers are to the left of zero. If you have 3 and -3, they are the same distance from zero but on opposite sides. When you add a number and its opposite, like 3 and -3, you get zero. People use negative numbers to show things like owing money or temperatures below freezing.
Rail transport\n\nRail transport is when people and things move in trains on tracks. Trains are long vehicles with wheels that roll on metal rails. The tracks are smooth and hard, so trains can carry very heavy loads without using too much energy. Trains can be pulled by engines that use diesel fuel or electricity. The first trains used steam power and were built in England a long time ago. Today, fast trains connect many cities in different countries. Trains help people travel and help shops get things to sell.
Potter's wheel\n\nA potter's wheel is a machine that spins around to help people make round bowls and pots out of clay. The potter puts a lump of soft clay on the wheel and pushes it with their hands while the wheel turns. The spinning clay takes shape into a cup, a plate, or a vase. Long ago, people made pots by rolling clay into long ropes and pinching them together. The potter's wheel made it faster and easier to make round shapes. Some old stories say that a god named Chnum made the first people on a potter's wheel.
Locust\n\nA locust is a kind of bug that looks like a grasshopper. Sometimes a huge group of locusts flies together. This group is called a swarm. A swarm can have many, many locusts. They eat all the green plants they find, like the food that farmers grow. This can hurt the plants and make it hard for people to get food. Locusts can fly very far and very fast. Some people eat locusts as food. Long ago, people wrote about locust swarms in stories.
Atmosphere\n\nAn atmosphere is a big blanket of air around a planet. The air is made of different gases. Gravity holds the air close to the planet so it does not float away into space. Earth has an atmosphere that lets us breathe and keeps us warm. The sky looks blue because of the atmosphere.
Sandpiper\n\nA sandpiper is a small bird that lives near water, like the ocean or a lake. It has a long, pointy beak and long legs. Sandpipers walk on the beach and poke their beaks into the wet sand to find tiny bugs and worms to eat. They have brown or gray feathers that help them hide. Sandpipers make a nest on the ground and lay three or four eggs. The babies can walk and find food soon after they hatch.
Coast\n\nThe coast is where the land meets the sea. It is the ground right next to the ocean. You can also call it the shore or the seaside. Many animals and plants live near the coast. Some people have houses on the coast. The coast can be sandy or rocky. Sometimes the water wears away the land slowly.
Imagination\n\nImagination is the power to make pictures in your mind. You can imagine a purple elephant or a castle in the clouds. When you pretend to be a superhero or a princess, you are using your imagination. It lets you think about things that are not real or not happening right now. Everyone has imagination, and it makes playtime fun.
Text to speech\n\nText to speech is a way for computers to read words out loud. A computer uses a special program to turn written words into spoken voice. People who cannot see well or have trouble reading can use text to speech to listen to books or websites. Long ago, people built machines that could make sounds like talking. Some machines used pipes and bellows to make vowel sounds. Today, computers learn from many voice samples to sound more natural and clear.
Tasmania\n\nTasmania is a big island near Australia. It is a state of Australia, like a part of the country. The biggest city is Hobart. Long ago, Tasmania was joined to the mainland, but then water came between them. Tasmania has lots of forests and trees. One special tree is the Leatherwood tree. Rare animals live there, like the Tasmanian devil and the eastern quoll. The thylacine, a striped animal, used to live there but is gone now. People from Europe came to live on the island. Tasmania has four cities: Hobart, Launceston, Devonport, and Burnie. It is the smallest state in Australia with about 500,000 people.
Matter\n\nMatter is everything around you that takes up space and has weight. It is made of tiny pieces called atoms. Atoms are so small you cannot see them. Matter can be a solid, like a rock or ice. It can be a liquid, like water or milk. It can also be a gas, like the air you breathe. When you heat matter, the atoms move faster and spread apart. When you cool it, they slow down and get closer. Your body, your toys, your food, and even the air are all made of matter.
American bison\n\nThe American bison is a big, furry animal that looks like a cow. It has a large head with small, curving horns. Its coat is long and shaggy on the front part of its body, and shorter on the back. Bison live in open grasslands and river valleys. They eat grass and other plants. Long ago, millions of bison lived in North America. People hunted many of them, and by 1890 only about 1,000 were left. Now there are more bison again, but not as many as before. You can see them in some national parks. The bison is the national animal of the United States. Some people raise bison for their meat, which is lean and a little sweet.
Potential energy\n\nPotential energy is energy that is stored and waiting to be used. It is like a ball sitting on a high shelf. The ball has energy because it is up high, and if it falls, that energy turns into moving energy. A stretched rubber band also has potential energy. When you let go, the rubber band flies across the room. A spring that is squeezed has potential energy too. When you let it go, it pops back out. Potential energy can change into moving energy, but the total amount of energy stays the same.
Common cold\n\nThe common cold is a sickness that makes your nose and throat feel bad. It is caused by tiny germs called viruses. You can get a cold when you are near someone who has it. The cold gives you a runny nose, a sore throat, a cough, and sometimes a fever. These feelings usually go away after about a week. There is no medicine that makes the cold go away, but you can rest and drink water to feel better. Washing your hands a lot helps stop the cold from spreading.
Zoroaster\n\nZoroaster was a man who lived a very long time ago in a place called Persia. He started a religion that many people followed. People who follow this religion believe in one God and try to be good. Zoroaster is a very important person in history.
Breakfast cereal\n\nBreakfast cereal is a food you eat in the morning. It is made from grains like wheat or corn. You pour it in a bowl and add milk. Many cereals taste sweet because they have sugar or fruit in them. Some cereals are for kids, like Cheerios or Cocoa Puffs. Other cereals are for grown-ups and help them stay healthy. A long time ago, people ate meat for breakfast. Then some people wanted to eat healthier, so they made the first cereal. It was called Granula and was very hard. You had to soak it in water all night before you could eat it. Later, two men named Mr. Kellogg and Mr. Post made their own cereals and started big companies.
Zulu people\n\nThe Zulu people are a group of people who live mostly in South Africa. There are many Zulu people, more than ten million. They speak a language called Zulu. Long ago, the Zulu had their own kingdom. Today, the Zulu people are the biggest group in South Africa and have the same rights as everyone else.
Persian language\n\nPersian is a language that people speak in some countries far away. It is also called Farsi. People in Iran, Afghanistan, and Tajikistan use this language to talk to each other. Some people in Pakistan and Uzbekistan speak it too. When you hear Persian, it sounds like a song because the words go up and down.
Belarus\n\nBelarus is a country in Eastern Europe. It is a big piece of land with many trees and forests. The capital city is Minsk. About nine million people live there. Belarus has many lakes and rivers. The land is mostly flat and has some marshy places. People in Belarus speak Belarusian and Russian. Most people are Belarusian, and some are Russian, Polish, or Ukrainian. The country was part of a bigger group called the Soviet Union until 1991. Now it is its own country. Belarus has a president named Alexander Lukashenko. The country helps Russia in a war with Ukraine. Belarus is a member of the United Nations.
Mass\n\nMass is how much stuff is in something. A big rock has more mass than a small pebble. Mass is not the same as weight. Weight changes if you go to the moon, but mass stays the same. You can measure mass with a scale. The more mass something has, the harder it is to push it. Big things like planets have a lot of mass, so they pull other things toward them. That pull is called gravity. We measure mass in grams and kilograms. A small apple has about 100 grams of mass. A big bag of rice has 1 kilogram of mass.
Engine\n\nAn engine is a machine that makes things move. It uses energy to create movement. Many cars have an engine inside. The engine burns fuel like petrol to make the car go. Some engines use steam, like old trains. Other engines use electricity, like some trains and toys. Engines can be big or small. They help us travel and do work.
Karate\n\nKarate is a way of fighting that comes from Japan. People who do karate use their hands, fists, elbows, legs, and knees to move and practice. Karate is not just about being strong. It also teaches you to have a strong mind and to be polite. People who do karate wear a white jacket and white pants called a Gi. They also wear a colored belt that shows how long they have been learning. A black belt means you have tried very hard for a long time. Karate became popular all over the world because of movies. Now many children and grown-ups learn karate for fun and to stay healthy.
Lakshmi\n\nLakshmi is a goddess in the Hindu religion. She is the goddess of money, wisdom, and good luck. Many people pray to her during Diwali, a big festival in India. Lakshmi has four arms and fair skin. She sits on a lotus flower and is often surrounded by elephants. She wears lots of jewelry. Her husband is the god Vishnu.
Optics\n\nOptics is the science of light. It tells us how rainbows happen and how light bounces off mirrors. Light can bend when it goes through water or glass. A prism can split light into many colors: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, and purple. Optics helps make glasses for people to see better, cameras to take pictures, telescopes to look at stars, and microscopes to see tiny things. All of these use lenses that focus light. New things are still learned in optics. Scientists made thin glass or plastic fibers that carry light very far. These fibers help send phone calls and the Internet all around the world.
Area\n\nArea is how much space a flat shape takes up. Think of a piece of paper or a floor. If you color a square on paper, the colored part is the area. Big shapes have more area than small shapes. We measure area in squares, like square feet or square meters. A square that is one foot on each side has an area of one square foot. Different shapes have different ways to find their area. For example, a circle has a lot of area but not much edge. A long skinny shape has a lot of edge but not much area.
Tasman Sea\n\nThe Tasman Sea is a big body of water between Australia and New Zealand. It is part of the Pacific Ocean. The sea was named after a man named Abel Tasman who explored it long ago. Some people call it 'The Ditch'.
Sudan\n\nSudan is a country in East Africa. Its biggest city is called Khartoum. Sudan has a sea next to it called the Red Sea. A big river called the Nile flows through Sudan and gives water to plants. Many people live in Sudan, and they are called Sudanese. Most people in Sudan speak Arabic. The most common religion in Sudan is Islam. Sudan used to be the biggest country in Africa, but part of it became a new country called South Sudan. Now Sudan is the third biggest country in Africa.
Highway\n\nA highway is a big road that helps people travel between cities and towns. Highways can have many lanes for cars to drive on. Some highways have a strip or wall in the middle to keep cars going opposite ways apart. Highways often have ramps and bridges to help cars get on and off. Many highways have numbers so people can find them easily. Sometimes too many cars on a highway make a traffic jam, which means cars have to go very slowly. Buses and special carpool lanes can help fix this problem.
Pancreas\n\nThe pancreas is a part inside your body. It is behind your tummy, on the left side. The pancreas helps break down food so your body can use it. It also makes special helpers that keep your blood healthy. If the pancreas stops working, a person can get very sick.
Trade\n\nTrade is when you give something to someone and they give you something else back. Long ago, people traded things without using money. That is called barter. Now, people often use money to buy and sell things. When you give money to get a toy, you are buying. When someone gives you money for something you made, you are selling. A place where people trade is called a market. Trade can happen between people, big companies, and even countries.
Lock (water navigation)\n\nA lock is a special place on a river or canal that helps boats go up or down when the water level changes. It is like a big box with doors at both ends. The lock can fill with water or let water out to make the boat go higher or lower. This helps boats travel even where there is a waterfall or a dam. Locks were first used a long time ago in China. Many locks are made of brick or stone.
Flax\n\nFlax is a plant with pretty flowers. People use the fibers from flax to make linen cloth. Some paper, like money paper, is also made from flax fibers. The seeds of flax can be pressed to make oil. Flax seeds are safe to eat in small amounts.
Flatworm\n\nA flatworm is a small animal with a soft, flat body. It has no bones inside. Flatworms live in water, like rivers and streams, or in damp places on land. Some flatworms are very tiny, smaller than your little finger. Many flatworms live on other animals and can make them sick. Some flatworms can hurt people, but doctors have medicine to help.
Brush\n\nA brush is a tool with bristles sticking out. Most brushes have a long handle to hold and a head that carries the bristles. We use brushes for cleaning, making hair look nice, and painting. A toothbrush is a brush for cleaning teeth. A paintbrush is for putting paint on paper or walls. Paintbrushes can be made from animal hair or man-made materials. They come in many sizes and shapes. Some brushes have wooden handles, and some have plastic handles.
Shiva\n\nShiva is a very important god in Hinduism. He is one of the three main gods, along with Brahma and Vishnu. Shiva is known as the destroyer, but he destroys bad things to make the world better. He has a blue neck because he once drank poison to save the world. Shiva has three eyes, and his third eye is on his forehead. He lives on a mountain called Mount Kailash with his wife Parvati and his two sons, Ganesha and Kartikeya. People pray to Shiva and call him by many names, like Mahadeva, which means "great god." He is often shown with a snake around his neck and a trident in his hand. Many people love Shiva because he is kind and easy to please.
Saga\n\nA saga is a long story from long ago. People in Iceland and other cold places told sagas. The sagas are about brave people who went on big boat trips and fought in battles. Some sagas are made up, and some are about real things that happened. The stories talk about families and friends and enemies. One famous saga is about a man named Njal. Sagas are fun to read because they feel like adventures.
Livestock\n\nLivestock are animals that people keep on farms. People use them for food like meat, milk, and eggs. Some livestock also give us wool for clothes. Cows, pigs, sheep, goats, and chickens are all livestock. Some big animals like horses and cows help people pull wagons. People have kept livestock for a very long time, since before there were cities. Today, most livestock live on big farms where many animals are kept together.
Weather front\n\nA weather front is where two big groups of air meet. One air group is warm and the other is cold. When they meet, it can make rain, storms, or wind. Sometimes the sky gets cloudy and rainy. After the front passes, the weather often gets clear and calm.
Puma\n\nA puma is a big wild cat. It is also called a cougar or mountain lion. Pumas live in North and South America. They are tan in color and can be very long, up to 9 feet. They cannot roar like a lion, but they can growl, hiss, and purr. Pumas eat only meat, like deer, rabbits, and squirrels. They hunt at night and are very good at sneaking up on their food. Baby pumas are called cubs. They live in mountains and forests and like to stay away from people.
Star\n\nA star is a very big ball of hot, bright stuff in space. The Sun is a star. It is the star closest to Earth. Stars give off light and heat. We see other stars in the night sky when the Sun goes down. Stars are made mostly of hydrogen. They are very old, usually billions of years. Some stars are big, some are small. The smallest stars are no bigger than a city. The biggest stars are huge. Stars are grouped into galaxies. Our galaxy is called the Milky Way. Stars help plants grow by giving light. The Earth and other planets go around the Sun. Stars can die. When a big star dies, it explodes. That is called a supernova. After a star dies, it can become a white dwarf, a neutron star, or a black hole.
Democratic Republic of the Congo\n\nThe Democratic Republic of the Congo is a big country in the middle of Africa. It is the second largest country in Africa. Many people live there, more than 71 million. The capital city is Kinshasa. The country has a long river called the Congo River that flows into the Atlantic Ocean. It has big forests and parks where animals like gorillas and okapis live. The country has had many wars and fights. Some groups still fight in the east. The United Nations helps keep peace there.
Old age\n\nOld age is when a person has lived for a very long time, usually 65 years or more. Old people often stop working and spend time helping take care of little children in their family. Their skin gets wrinkly, and they move slower and feel cold more often. Old people have more health problems than young people, and many take medicine. Their bones can get weak, and some cannot see or hear well. Old people are also called elders. Many people think elders are wise because they have learned a lot in their long lives. In many places, people are kind to elders and learn from them.
Conifer\n\nConifers are plants that make seeds inside cones. Most conifers are trees, and some are small bushes. They have leaves that look like needles or scales. Conifers stay green all year long. You can find them in many places around the world, especially in cold forests called taiga. People use the wood from conifers to build houses and make paper. Some conifers are very tall, like redwoods. Others, like pines, have a nice smell. Conifers are very old plants. They were alive when dinosaurs walked on Earth.
Healthcare\n\nHealthcare is when doctors and nurses help people stay healthy or get better when they are sick. A doctor checks your body, gives you medicine, and tells you how to feel good. Hospitals are big buildings where very sick people go to get help. Doctors also help people who feel sad or worried in their mind. Keeping people healthy costs money, and different countries spend different amounts on healthcare.
Electrical generator\n\nAn electrical generator is a machine that makes electricity. It has wires that spin around inside a special magnet. When the wires spin, electricity flows through them. Some generators are small and you can turn them with your hands or feet. Bigger ones are turned by an engine. The biggest ones are in power stations and use steam or water to spin. Some generators use wind to spin. A generator turns moving energy into electricity. Some generators have a gas engine and are dangerous to use inside because they make bad air that can hurt you.
Cleveland\n\nCleveland is a big city in Ohio, United States. It sits next to a big lake called Lake Erie. Many people live there. Long ago, Cleveland was a place where trains and boats brought things to make in factories. Today, it is known for its music and sports. The Cleveland Orchestra plays beautiful music. The Rock and Roll Hall of Fame is a museum about rock music. People watch baseball with the Cleveland Indians, football with the Cleveland Browns, and basketball with the Cleveland Cavaliers. The city also has a famous hospital called the Cleveland Clinic that helps sick people get better.
Indonesian language\n\nIndonesian language is the main language of Indonesia, a country far away. People use it to talk to each other all over the country. Kids learn it in school, and it is used on TV and radio. Many people in Indonesia also speak their own family language at home. Indonesian language has words from other languages like Dutch, English, Chinese, and Arabic because people from faraway places came to trade long ago.
Bharata Natyam\n\nBharata Natyam is a special dance from India. Both boys and girls can do this dance. It tells stories from old Indian tales. The dancers move their hands and feet in careful ways. They also make faces to show feelings like happy or sad. People in India and other countries like to watch and learn this dance. It comes from a place called Tamil Nadu. A long time ago, dancers did this dance in temples. Today, many people still practice and perform Bharata Natyam.
Invertebrate\n\nAn invertebrate is an animal that does not have a backbone. Most animals in the world are invertebrates. Insects are invertebrates. They have a hard skin on the outside of their bodies instead of bones inside. Spiders, worms, and snails are also invertebrates. They come in many shapes and sizes.
Violin\n\nA violin is a wooden instrument that makes music. It has four strings and a long stick called a bow. You hold the violin under your chin and move the bow across the strings to make sound. Your left hand presses the strings to make different notes. The violin is the smallest instrument in its family and makes high sounds. People who play the violin are called violinists. Some violins are very old and cost a lot of money. The violin is used in many kinds of music, like classical, folk, and even jazz. It takes a long time to learn how to play well.
American robin\n\nThe American robin is a bird that lives in North America. It has a round body, long legs, and a long tail. Its chest is orange-red, and its back is gray-brown. The American robin sings in the morning. It eats worms, bugs, and berries. It builds a nest with grass and mud in a tree. The mother lays blue eggs. Both parents feed the babies until they can fly. You can see American robins in gardens, parks, and fields.
Taxi\n\nA taxi is a car that people can ride to go where they want. You tell the driver where you want to go, and they take you there. Taxis are different from buses because they do not stop for other people along the way. You pay money for the ride, and the price depends on how far you go. Many big cities have taxis. The first taxis were horse-drawn carriages in Paris and London a long time ago. Later, a machine called a taximeter was invented to measure how much the ride costs.
Electrical grid\n\nAn electrical grid is a big net of wires that brings electricity to your house. The wires carry power from a power plant, where electricity is made, all the way to the lights and toys you use. The grid connects many houses and buildings together so everyone can have electricity.
Civil rights movements\n\nCivil rights movements are times when many people work together to make sure everyone is treated fairly. People in these movements want all people to have the same rights, no matter what they look like or who they are. Sometimes people use peaceful ways, like marching and sitting still, to show they want change. Other times, people fight. Many of these movements helped make things better, even if they did not get everything they wanted. In the United States, black people were kept apart from white people in schools, buses, and restaurants. This was called segregation. Rosa Parks did not give up her seat on a bus to a white person, and she was arrested. Then many black people stopped riding the buses for over a year. A man named Martin Luther King, Jr. helped lead these peaceful protests. Finally, the law said black people could sit anywhere on the bus. Other movements worked for the rights of Mexican Americans, Native Americans, women, and people who love someone of the same gender.
Koala\n\nA koala is a small animal that lives in trees in Australia. It has soft gray or brown fur, a big black nose, and sharp claws for climbing. Koalas are not bears, even though they look like teddy bears. They sleep a lot, about 20 hours each day, because they eat leaves that give them very little energy. Koalas eat leaves from eucalyptus trees, which are poisonous to most animals, but koalas have special helpers in their tummy that make the poison safe. They almost never drink water because they get all the water they need from the leaves. On hot days, koalas cool down by hugging a tree trunk. A baby koala is very tiny when it is born, smaller than your thumb, and it crawls into its mother's pouch. It stays there for about a year until it is big enough to eat leaves on its own. Koalas live alone and are awake mostly at night.
Fencing\n\nFencing is a sport where two people use special swords. The goal is to touch the other person with the sword to score a point. There is a referee who watches. Fencers wear white clothes to stay safe. They wear a mask with a black mesh to protect their face. They also wear a jacket, pants, and long socks. Some swords are light and bendy, and some are heavy. Fencers try to hit different parts of the body depending on the sword they use.
Witness\n\nA witness is a person who sees something happen. When people go to court to find out the truth, witnesses tell what they saw. They promise to tell the truth. If a witness lies, that is a bad thing and they can get in trouble. Sometimes a witness has to go to court even if they do not want to.
Morse code\n\nMorse code is a way to send messages using short and long signals. Short signals are called 'dits' and long signals are called 'dahs'. People used to send Morse code with lights, sounds, or radio. For example, the letters S.O.S. are three dits, three dahs, and three dits. Ships used S.O.S. when they needed help. Today, not many people use Morse code, but some still do for fun.
Jaguar\n\nA jaguar is a big cat with spots. It lives in South America and Central America. Jaguars have yellow or orange fur with brown and black spots. Some jaguars are all black, but you can still see the spots if you look close. They are very strong and have a powerful bite. Jaguars like to stay near water and are good at swimming. They hunt alone and eat many animals like fish, birds, and even turtles. A mother jaguar has one to four babies at a time. The babies stay with her for one or two years. Jaguars can live up to 12 years in the wild and up to 22 years in a zoo.
Wildebeest\n\nA wildebeest is a big animal that lives in Africa. It has four legs and hooves, like a cow. Wildebeests eat grass. They move from place to place to find grass to eat. In May, many wildebeests walk from the grasslands to the woods. In November, they walk back. Baby wildebeests are born in the summer. Big cats like lions and cheetahs hunt wildebeests for food. Wildebeests can live for more than 20 years.
Atom\n\nAn atom is a very, very tiny piece of everything. Everything around you, like toys, water, and air, is made of atoms. Atoms are so small that you cannot see them, even with a strong magnifying glass. Scientists use special tools to learn about atoms. An atom has three main parts: protons, neutrons, and electrons. Protons and neutrons are in the middle, called the nucleus. Electrons move very fast around the nucleus. There are over 100 different kinds of atoms, called elements. Gold and carbon are examples of elements. Atoms can stick together to make bigger things, like water. A water molecule is made of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom. Atoms can also break apart, which makes energy. This happens inside stars and in nuclear power plants.
Giant panda\n\nA giant panda is a bear with black and white fur. It lives in the mountains of China. The black fur is on its ears, around its eyes, on its legs, and on its shoulders. Giant pandas eat bamboo almost all the time. They spend 10 to 16 hours each day eating bamboo. They also drink water from streams in the mountains. Baby pandas are called cubs. A cub stays with its mother for up to three years. Giant pandas are very special and protected by the Chinese government. They are in danger because people are cutting down the forests where they live.
Television\n\nA television is a machine with a screen that shows pictures and makes sounds. It can look like a box or a flat rectangle. Old TVs were big and heavy, but new TVs are light and flat. The TV gets signals from far away and turns them into shows you can watch. You can see cartoons, movies, and news on a TV. Some TVs show colors, but old ones only showed black and white. People also use TVs to play video games.
Orphan\n\nAn orphan is a child who has no mom or dad. Sometimes the parents die, and sometimes they cannot take care of the child. Some orphans live in a special house called an orphanage. Other orphans go to live with a new family. That is called adoption. Some stories have orphans, like Harry Potter and Annie.
Mirage\n\nA mirage is a trick your eyes see outside. It makes things look different from what they really are. This happens because light bends when it goes through hot and cold air. Sometimes the ground looks like it has water on it, but it is just a mirage. Other times, a ship or an island might look like it is floating in the sky. That is also a mirage. The word "mirage" comes from a word that means "to look at."
Portuguese language\n\nPortuguese is a language that people speak in many countries. It started in a place called Portugal a long time ago. Now many people speak it in Brazil, Angola, Mozambique, and other places around the world. Portuguese and English have some words that sound alike, like 'cobra' and 'mosquito.' Some English words come from Portuguese, like 'tank' and 'coconut.' People in different countries speak Portuguese a little differently, but they can still understand each other.
Polytheism\n\nPolytheism is when people believe in many gods. Long ago, the Greeks and Romans had many gods. Some people today still believe in many gods, like in Shinto or Wicca. These religions have stories about their gods, called myths. The opposite is believing in just one god.
Shipbuilding\n\nShipbuilding is the job of making big boats called ships. Long ago, people built many ships in places like Glasgow and Sunderland. Today, most ships are built in countries like South Korea and China. Japan used to build the most ships, but now it is in third place.
City-state\n\nA city-state is a city that is its own country. Long ago, there were many city-states in a place called Greece. A city-state makes its own rules and collects its own money. Today, only a few places like Singapore are city-states.
Relic\n\nA relic is a special old thing that people keep because it reminds them of someone very important. Some relics are parts of a person's body, like a tooth or a bone. Other relics are things that person used, like a cup or a piece of clothing. People treat relics with great care and respect. Many religions have relics, like the Tooth of Buddha or the Crown of Thorns. A special box that holds a relic is called a reliquary.
Boxing\n\nBoxing is a sport where two people fight in a special square called a ring. They wear big soft gloves on their hands. The fighters try to hit each other but not too hard. A fight can end when one fighter falls down and cannot get up for ten seconds. That is called a knockout. Sometimes the fight stops because one fighter is too hurt to keep going. Other times, the winner is the one who hits the other more times. If both fighters are even, the fight is a draw, like a tie. Each round is three minutes for men and two minutes for women.
Hearing\n\nHearing is how you listen to sounds. Your ears feel tiny shakes in the air called sounds. Most animals can hear. Land animals with backbones hear through their ears. Fish hear in other ways, like with a special part of their body. In animals like you, sound goes through three parts of the ear: the outside part, the middle part, and the inside part.
Legendary creature\n\nA legendary creature is a made-up animal that people tell stories about. These creatures are not real, but they are in fairy tales, myths, and old stories. Some famous ones are dragons that breathe fire, unicorns with one horn on their head, and mermaids that are half fish and half person. People have been telling stories about these creatures for a very long time.
Emu\n\nAn emu is a very tall bird that cannot fly. It lives in Australia. The emu is the second tallest bird in the world, after the ostrich. Emus have soft brown feathers that keep them cool. They have long legs with three toes on each foot. Their wings are very short and hidden under their feathers. Emus can run very fast. They eat plants, seeds, flowers, and insects. The father emu sits on the eggs until they hatch. Baby emus have stripes on their feathers that help hide them. Emus can live for 10 to 20 years.
Funeral\n\nA funeral is a special gathering when someone has died. Friends and family come together to feel sad and to remember the good things about that person. The dead body is usually in a box called a coffin. Sometimes people can see the body, and sometimes they cannot. After the funeral, the body is buried in the ground or burned into ashes. People may say a prayer to wish the person peace. Funerals can be held in a church, a temple, or another place. Some families bring pictures or favorite things to remember the person. In some places, people have different traditions, like dancing with bones or having a party to celebrate the person's life.
Town\n\nA town is a place with many houses, but it is smaller than a city and bigger than a village. People in towns often work in factories, shops, or for the town, not on farms. Some towns have a market where people buy and sell things. In different countries, the rules for what makes a town are not the same. For example, in some parts of the United States, a town is a part of a county, and people can vote at town meetings to decide things. In other places, a town is just a name for any place where many people live.
Triceratops\n\nTriceratops was a huge dinosaur that ate only plants. It lived a long time ago in North America. Its name means "three-horned face" because it had three horns on its head. Two long horns were above its eyes, and one short horn was on its nose. It also had a big bony shield behind its head to protect its neck. Triceratops was as long as a big car and as heavy as two elephants. It walked on four strong legs and had a beak like a bird to bite off leaves and plants. Its mouth was full of many teeth that helped it chew tough plants. Triceratops used its horns to fight with other dinosaurs, like the scary Tyrannosaurus. Sometimes Triceratops got hurt but then got better. Baby Triceratops were called hatchlings and grew up to be big and strong.
Maple\n\nA maple is a kind of tree or bush. Maple trees have leaves with sharp points. The leaves turn bright colors in the fall. Maple trees grow in many places like Asia, Europe, and North America. Maple trees make a special fruit that spins like a helicopter when it falls. People plant maple trees in cities because they look pretty. Some maple trees give us sweet syrup for pancakes. The flag of Canada has a maple leaf on it.
Antarctica\n\nAntarctica is the coldest place on Earth. It is at the very bottom of the world, near the South Pole. Almost all of Antarctica is covered by a thick layer of ice. No people live there all the time, but some scientists stay for a while to study. The animals that live there are penguins, seals, and tiny bugs. Penguins are birds that cannot fly, but they swim very well. They have black and white feathers that keep them warm. The biggest penguins can be as tall as a four-year-old child. Antarctica is also very dry, like a desert, and very windy. It is a special place where only animals and plants that like cold can live.
Storm\n\nA storm is very strong weather with a lot of rain and wind. Sometimes there is also hail, which is ice that falls from the sky, and lightning, which is a big flash of light. Thunder is the loud noise that comes with lightning. Some storms are so strong they have special names, like hurricane or tornado. Storms can happen in many places and can be very powerful.
Transformer\n\nA transformer is a machine that moves electricity from one wire to another without the wires touching. It uses a special force called a magnetic field to do this. Transformers come in many sizes. Some are tiny and live inside microphones. Others are huge and help send electricity all over the city. The main job of a transformer is to change the push of electricity. High push is good for sending electricity far away. Low push is safe for your home. You can see transformers on power poles in your neighborhood. They take the strong electricity from the big wires and make it weaker so it can run your lights, TV, and refrigerator. Inside your toys and computers, tiny transformers help give each part the right amount of electricity.
Bone fracture\n\nA bone fracture is when a bone gets a crack or breaks. Bones are usually very strong, but if something hits them too hard, they can break. Sometimes the broken bone stays inside the skin, and sometimes it pokes through the skin. When the bone pokes through, it can let germs in and cause an ouchie. Doctors take a picture called an X-ray to see the break. To fix it, they line up the broken pieces and keep them still so the bone can grow back together. It takes about 6 to 8 weeks for a bone to heal.
Central Park\n\nCentral Park is a very big park in New York City. It is in a part of the city called Manhattan. Many people visit Central Park every year. The park has lakes, a castle, a zoo, and a big museum. You can walk, run, or ride a bike there. There are also playgrounds and fields to play on. Central Park is so big that it is bigger than some small countries. Many movies and TV shows show Central Park.
Algae\n\nAlgae are plant-like living things that make their own food from sunlight. They are very old and lived long before other plants. Algae can be very small, with just one cell, or very big, like seaweed in the ocean. They live in wet places like ponds, lakes, and the sea. Some algae float in the water and are called phytoplankton. Many fish and sea animals eat algae. Some algae grow into big underwater forests called kelp forests. These forests give homes to sea otters, sea urchins, and other animals. People also use some algae as food or to make things like jelly. Sometimes too many algae grow and make a big green or red patch on the water. This can be bad for fish.
Spine\n\nYour spine is the long row of bones in the middle of your back. It is also called your backbone. The spine helps you stand up straight and bend. Inside the spine is a special tube that holds your nerves. Animals with a spine are called vertebrates. You are a vertebrate because you have a spine. Sometimes people get a sore back, and that can hurt.
Catapult\n\nA catapult is a big machine that throws heavy rocks or other things through the air. Long ago, people used catapults to break castle walls or set things on fire. A catapult works by using a heavy weight and a long arm to fling things far away. Today, catapults are not used for fighting anymore. You can see old catapults in museums. Some people build small catapults for fun or for school experiments. Big ships called aircraft carriers use a special kind of catapult to help airplanes take off.
Colour theory\n\nColour theory is a set of ideas about how colors work together. It helps us mix colors and make pretty pictures. There are three main colors called primary colors: red, yellow, and blue. When you mix two primary colors, you get a secondary color. For example, mixing yellow and blue makes green. Mixing red and blue makes purple. Mixing red and yellow makes orange. Colors can look different depending on the light. A yellow toy might look green or brown next to a bright white wall. Paint colors mix differently than light colors. You cannot make brown by mixing colored lights. Color theory helps artists and people who design things choose colors that look nice together.
Greek alphabet\n\nThe Greek alphabet is a set of 24 letters used to write the Greek language. People also use Greek letters in math and science to stand for numbers or ideas. Many letters in the Greek alphabet look like letters in the English alphabet. The Greek alphabet is very old, and many other alphabets came from it. Long ago, the Greeks borrowed letters from another alphabet and changed them to fit their own language. They also added special marks to show how to say words. Today, the Greek alphabet is still used in Greece.
Pastry\n\nPastry is a kind of dough that people use to make baked foods. Dough is a soft mix of flour, butter, sugar, milk, and eggs. You roll it flat and then bake it in the oven. Pastry can be used to make pies, tarts, and little cakes. Some pastries are sweet, and some are not sweet. Many people like to eat pastries for a treat.
Conceptual art\n\nConceptual art is a kind of art where the idea is more important than how it looks. Sometimes the artist writes down instructions for anyone to follow to make the art. This art can be made of words or things you find around you. It asks questions like 'What is art?' and 'Who can be an artist?' Conceptual artists do not always paint or make sculptures. They might use words, photos, or everyday objects to share their ideas.
Mango\n\nA mango is a fruit that grows on a tree. It is very sweet when it is ripe, but it tastes sour before it is ready to eat. Mangoes come in many different kinds, like Alphonso. They grow in warm places like India and Pakistan. People eat mangoes as a snack or in desserts. The tree that grows mangoes can also be used to make wood for things like furniture and musical instruments.
Lebanon\n\nLebanon is a country next to the Mediterranean Sea. It is in the Middle East. Lebanon has mountains and a long coast. The capital city is Beirut. Many people live in Lebanon. The official language is Arabic. The cedar tree is a special symbol of Lebanon because many cedar trees grow in the mountains.
Polish language\n\nPolish is a language that people speak in Poland. It is the main language there. Many people also speak Polish in other countries like the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom. Polish has some letters that look like English letters but have marks above or below them. Some Polish sounds are different from English. For example, Polish "w" sounds like English "v". Polish words are said with a little more force on the second-to-last part. You can say "Dzień dobry" for "Good morning" and "Cześć" for "Hi" or "Bye".
Pope\n\nA pope is the leader of the Catholic Church. He lives in a small country called Vatican City. The pope wears special white clothes and a tall hat. He is chosen by cardinals, who are important church helpers. Once chosen, the pope is the leader for a very long time, sometimes for his whole life. The pope travels to many countries to talk about peace and love. He is protected by guards wearing colorful uniforms. People call him 'father' because the word 'pope' means father in an old language.
History of the Earth\n\nThe history of the Earth is the story of how our planet came to be and changed over a very, very long time. Earth is very old—about 4.56 billion years old. That is much older than any person or animal. A long time ago, Earth was not here yet. It started as a big, spinning cloud of dust and gas in space. The dust and gas slowly came together to make Earth. At first, Earth was very hot, like a big ball of melted rock. Then, a giant rock from space hit Earth. That crash made a lot of dust and rock fly into space, and that dust and rock came together to make the Moon. The Moon is our big, round neighbor in the sky. After that, Earth cooled down and got a hard outer shell. The first tiny living things appeared in the water about 3.5 billion years ago. They were very small, like little blobs. Over millions of years, more and more kinds of plants and animals grew on Earth. The land moved around, and big pieces called continents slowly drifted. Today, Earth has oceans, land, air, and many living things, including people.
Mulberry\n\nA mulberry is a kind of tree. It grows in warm places in Asia, Africa, and the Americas. The tree has leaves that are simple and sometimes have bumps. The fruit grows in bunches and is red or dark purple. You can eat the fruit, and it tastes sweet. People use the fruit to make pies, tarts, and wine. The leaves of the white mulberry tree are food for silkworms. Silkworms make silk from their cocoons. The white mulberry tree can shoot its pollen very fast, faster than any other plant.
Fly\n\nA fly is a small insect that can fly. It has two wings on its body and two tiny knobs that help it balance in the air. Flies have big eyes that let them see all around. They are very fast fliers and can dodge and turn quickly to escape from danger. A fly starts as an egg, then becomes a grub that eats a lot, then turns into a pupa, and finally becomes an adult fly. There are many kinds of flies all over the world.
Malay Peninsula\n\nThe Malay Peninsula is a big piece of land that sticks out into the ocean in Southeast Asia. It is long and narrow, like a finger. Three different parts of the peninsula belong to different countries. Many people live there, and the land is covered with green forests and warm beaches.
Party\n\nA party is when people get together to have fun. Sometimes a party is for a birthday, a holiday, or just because. At a party, there are friends, games, and yummy food. People laugh, talk, and play together. Some parties have balloons, music, and cake. A party makes everyone feel happy.
Pink\n\nPink is a light red color. You can make pink paint by mixing red paint with white paint. Pink is a very easy color to make. Many flowers are pink, like roses. Some people like to wear pink clothes. Pink can be a soft and pretty color.
Harrow (tool)\n\nA harrow is a farm tool that breaks up dirt on the ground. It makes the soil smooth and soft for planting seeds. A plow digs deep into the dirt, but a harrow works on the top. It breaks up big clumps of dirt and takes out weeds. Some harrows have round metal discs, and some have teeth or chains. Long ago, horses or people pulled harrows. Now, tractors pull them. Farmers use harrows to get the soil ready for planting.
Swan\n\nA swan is a big water bird that lives on ponds, lakes, and rivers. Swans have long necks, big feet, and large wings. Most swans are white, but some are black or have black necks. They eat plants from the bottom of the water, and also eat bugs and small animals. A baby swan is called a cygnet. Swans are very strong and protect their babies. They can fly very far to find warm places in winter.
Quiz\n\nA quiz is a game where you answer questions. You can play by yourself or with a team. Each right answer gives you points. The person with the most points wins. Teachers sometimes use quizzes to help you learn new things.
Hiking\n\nHiking is walking outside in nature, like in the woods or on a mountain. Some people hike for one day and come back home before dark. Other people hike for many days and sleep outside. Hikers like to see pretty trees, flowers, and animals. They also like to breathe fresh air. Before a hike, you need to plan. You should look at a map and check the weather. You need to bring water, food, and a backpack. It is safer to hike with a friend, not alone. If you get lost, stop and use a map or a compass to find your way.
Natural History Museum\n\nThe Natural History Museum is a big place in London where you can see lots of things from nature. It has huge collections of rocks, bones of old animals called fossils, and stuffed animals and plants. You can see a giant dinosaur skeleton there. The museum also has scientists who study these things. It is one of the biggest museums of its kind in Britain.
Atmosphere of Earth\n\nThe atmosphere of Earth is the air all around our planet. It is made of gases that stay close to Earth because of gravity. The air we breathe has mostly nitrogen and oxygen. There is also a little bit of argon, carbon dioxide, and water vapor. The atmosphere protects us from the sun's hot rays. It keeps our days from getting too hot and our nights from getting too cold. The air gets thinner the higher you go. Most of the air is near the ground. The atmosphere has different layers, like an onion. Near the ground, the air is thick and cold. Higher up, in the stratosphere, there is a special layer called the ozone layer that blocks harmful sun rays. Even higher, the air is very thin and only light gases like helium and hydrogen are left. The atmosphere also has tiny bits of dust and ash that help make clouds and fog.
Second\n\nA second is a very short amount of time. It is how we measure time. There are 60 seconds in one minute. One heartbeat of a grown-up at rest lasts about one second. Scientists use a special kind of clock to measure a second very exactly. That clock counts how fast a tiny thing called an atom wiggles. The atom wiggles about 9 billion times in one second. A second is so short that you can say "one second" in the time it takes.
Old World vulture\n\nOld World vultures are big birds that eat dead animals. They are in the same bird family as eagles and hawks. These vultures find their food only by looking with their eyes. They have bald heads with no long feathers. This helps them stay clean when they eat. Some vultures eat fruit from palm trees instead of dead animals.
Molecule\n\nA molecule is the smallest piece of a thing that can still be that thing. If you break it into even smaller pieces, it becomes something else. Molecules are made of tiny parts called atoms that stick together. In air, molecules fly around. In water, they are stuck together but can still move. In sugar, they only wiggle in place. Atoms stick together by sharing tiny bits called electrons. When you heat a molecule, the atoms move more and the bond can break. Some molecules give off energy when they break, like a candle that burns.
History of Christianity\n\nThe history of Christianity is about how the Christian religion began and grew. It started with a man named Jesus and his twelve friends, called apostles. Jesus lived a long time ago in a place called Judea. After Jesus died, his friends told everyone about him. At first, only Jewish people followed Jesus, but soon other people did too. The followers were called Christians. For a long time, the Roman leaders did not like Christians and sometimes hurt them. But later, a Roman emperor named Constantine said people could be Christians. Then another emperor made Christianity the main religion of Rome. Over time, Christianity spread to many places around the world. Today it is the biggest religion. Christians believe in one God and that Jesus is God's son. They go to church, sing songs, and pray. They have special books called the Bible, which has two parts: the Old Testament and the New Testament.
Landform\n\nA landform is a shape on the ground. Some landforms are big, and some are small. Hills, mountains, valleys, and plains are all landforms. A hill is a bump of land. A mountain is a very tall hill. A valley is the low land between hills. A plain is flat land. Water can make landforms by moving dirt and rocks. Wind can also change the shape of land over a long time.
Tunisia\n\nTunisia is a country in Africa, near the Mediterranean Sea. The capital city is Tunis. Many people live in Tunisia and speak a language called Tunisian Arabic. The country has a big desert called the Sahara, and also green land where farmers grow fruits and vegetables. People visit Tunisia to see the beach and the desert. Tunisia became its own country in 1956.
Gazelle\n\nA gazelle is a kind of animal that lives in Africa and Asia. It has long legs and can run very fast for a long time. Gazelles live in big groups called herds. They eat grass and leaves from plants. When a lion or cheetah chases them, they run slowly and jump high in the air. That is how they get away.
Paran River\n\nThe Paran River is a very long river in South America. It flows through Brazil, Paraguay, and Argentina. It is the second longest river in South America, after the Amazon River. The name Paran means "like the sea" in an old language. The river starts in Brazil where two smaller rivers join together. It flows south and joins other rivers before reaching the big ocean. People fish for surub and sbalo in the river. There are big dams on the river that make electricity.
Seahorse\n\nA seahorse is a small fish that lives in warm ocean water. Its head looks like a horse's head, and that is how it got its name. Seahorses can change color to hide from other animals. The daddy seahorse is special because he carries the eggs in a pouch on his belly until the babies are ready to come out. When the babies are born, they are very tiny and have to take care of themselves. Seahorses swim standing up and use their curly tail to hold onto plants in the water.
Hagia Sophia\n\nHagia Sophia is a big building in Istanbul, Turkey. It was first a church a long time ago, then it became a mosque, and later it was a museum. Now it is a mosque again. The building has a very big round roof called a dome. The walls and floor are very old, and there are pretty pictures made of tiny colored stones on the walls. Many people visit Hagia Sophia to see how old and beautiful it is.
World Wide Web\n\nThe World Wide Web is a part of the Internet where you can look at websites and webpages. It was made by a man named Tim Berners-Lee in 1989. He wanted scientists to share papers easily. To see the Web, you need a computer or phone with a web browser like Chrome or Safari. The browser asks a web server for a page, and the server sends it back. Web pages are written in a special code called HTML. They can have words, pictures, videos, and links. When you click a link, it takes you to another page. The Web helps people learn, play, and talk to each other.
Truffle\n\nA truffle is a special kind of mushroom that grows underground, near the roots of trees like oak and hazel. Truffles smell very strong and taste yummy, so people use them in cooking to make food taste better. Some truffles are black and some are white. They are very hard to find, so they cost a lot of money. People use trained dogs or pigs to sniff out truffles from the ground. The pigs like truffles because they smell like another pig. Black truffles grow in winter, and white truffles grow in autumn. The biggest truffle ever found was as heavy as a small dog.
Brick\n\nA brick is a hard block that people use to build walls and walkways. Bricks are made mostly from clay, which is a kind of dirt. The clay is shaped into a brick and then baked in a very hot oven until it becomes hard. Bricks can be different colors, like red, brown, or gray, depending on the clay. Workers called masons stack bricks on top of each other and stick them together with a special paste called mortar. Bricks have been used for a very long time, even thousands of years ago. They are strong and last a long time, especially when they are baked. Most bricks are about the same size so that a worker can hold one in one hand.
Gender\n\nGender is a word about how people show if they feel more like a boy, a girl, or something else. Long ago, people only used the word 'gender' for words in sentences, not for people. Now, some people use 'gender' to talk about how they feel inside, and 'sex' to talk about their body. A person's gender can be different from their body. Some people feel like a boy, some feel like a girl, and some feel like both or neither. People can show their gender by the clothes they wear, the way they talk, and the things they like to do. Many years ago, most people thought there were only two genders: boy and girl. But now, more people know that there are many ways to be. Some people use the word 'they' for someone who does not feel like a boy or a girl. Everyone gets to choose how they want to be called.
Yeast\n\nYeast is a tiny living thing that is too small to see with just your eyes. It is a kind of fungus, like the stuff that grows on old bread. Yeast likes to eat sugar. When it eats sugar, it makes bubbles of gas. People put yeast in bread dough, and the bubbles make the bread get big and fluffy. Yeast is also used to make some drinks. Most yeast makes more yeast by making a little bud that grows into a new yeast.
Taro\n\nTaro is a plant that people eat as a vegetable. The part we eat is the stem, which grows under the ground. People also eat the leaves. Taro grows in places like islands in the ocean. Long ago, people started growing taro as one of the first plants they took care of. You must cook taro before you eat it, because it is not safe to eat raw. After cooking, it is soft and good to eat.
Indian philosophy\n\nIndian philosophy is the way people in India think about big questions like what is real and how to live. These ideas are very old, from more than two thousand years ago. Some of these philosophies believe in old holy books called the Vedas, and some do not. The ones that believe in the Vedas are called stika, and the ones that do not are called nstika. Buddhism and Jainism are two famous philosophies that do not follow the Vedas. People who study Indian philosophy talk about many things, like how to be good, what happens after we die, and how to find peace.
Smoking (cooking)\n\nSmoking is a way to cook food so it stays good longer. People use it for meat and fish. The food is put near the smoke from a fire. The smoke takes some water out of the food and gives it a yummy taste. Smoking also changes how the food feels in your mouth.
Bolero\n\nBolero is a kind of slow music and dance. People move slowly and gently to the music. The music is played with a guitar. Dancers hold each other and step together. It comes from Spain and Cuba.
Vikings\n\nVikings were people from far north in Europe, from places called Norway, Sweden, and Denmark. They were very good at building boats called longships. These boats could go in shallow water, so Vikings could travel up rivers and attack towns. They raided many places in Europe, like England and France, from about 700 to 1100 years ago. Vikings were strong fighters and people were scared of them. Some Vikings settled in new lands and started farms and villages. They also traveled across the ocean to Iceland, Greenland, and even to a place in Canada. Vikings had many gods, like Odin and Thor. They celebrated a holiday called Yuletide, which later became Christmas. Real Vikings did not wear helmets with horns, even though some stories show them that way.
Demeter\n\nDemeter is a make-believe goddess from old Greek stories. She took care of plants and helped farmers grow food like wheat and bread. Demeter had a daughter named Persephone. One day, a king of the underworld took Persephone away. Demeter was very sad, and the earth became cold and nothing would grow. When Persephone came back, the earth got warm and plants grew again. That is why we have seasons: winter when Demeter is sad, and summer when she is happy.
History of Australia\n\nThe history of Australia is a very long story. The first people lived in Australia more than 65,000 years ago. They are called Aboriginals and Torres Strait Islanders. They hunted animals, fished in the water, and picked food from the land. They made special tools like the boomerang and the spear. They told stories about how the world was made, called the Dreamtime. They painted these stories on rocks and walls. They also made music with a special instrument called the didgeridoo.\n\nLater, people from Europe came to Australia on big ships. The first was a Dutch explorer in 1606. Then in 1770, a British sailor named Captain James Cook found the east coast and said it belonged to Britain. The British sent ships with people who had been in jail to live in Australia. These people were called convicts. The first ships came in 1788. Life was very hard at first because there was not much food. But soon people started farms and towns grew. People found gold in 1851, and many people came to look for it. Some became very rich.\n\nOver time, the people in Australia wanted to make their own rules. They started voting for their leaders. In 1901, all the parts of Australia came together as one country. In the 21st century, Julia Gillard became the first woman to be the leader of Australia.
Great Dividing Range\n\nThe Great Dividing Range is a very long line of mountains in Australia. It runs all along the east side of the country, from the north to the south. These mountains are not just one big mountain; they are many hills, flat places, and steep cliffs all together. The mountains make the clouds drop lots of rain on the east side, so the land there is green and wet. The highest mountain in the range is called Mount Kosciuszko, and it is very tall. Many parts of the range are inside parks where people can walk, play, and see animals.
Taj Mahal\n\nThe Taj Mahal is a big, beautiful building in India. It is made of white stone and looks like a giant palace with a round top. A king named Shah Jahan built it a long time ago for his wife. Many people visit the Taj Mahal every year because it is so pretty. The building looks pink in the morning, yellow in the evening, and gold at night. But the air is making it turn yellow, and that is not good for the building.
Mayonnaise\n\nMayonnaise is a thick, creamy sauce. It is made from oil and egg yolk, with a little lemon juice or vinegar. People put it on sandwiches, salads, and french fries to make them taste good.
Water cycle\n\nThe water cycle is how water moves around the Earth. Water goes up into the sky from the ground and from rivers and oceans. It makes clouds. Then the water falls back down as rain or snow. The rain fills up rivers and lakes. Then the water goes up again. This keeps happening over and over. Water is very important for all living things on Earth.
Speech\n\nSpeech is when people talk to each other. Only people can talk. Animals make sounds, but they do not talk like we do. When you speak, sounds come from your throat and are shaped by your mouth, tongue, teeth, and lips. Sometimes people have trouble speaking, and a helper can teach them how to talk better.
Slang\n\nSlang are special words that some people use. Different groups of people have their own slang. For example, kids might use words that grown-ups do not understand. Grown-ups might use old words that kids think are funny. Over time, slang words can become normal words that everyone uses. Some slang words are short, like 'wassup' for 'how are you?' and 'dunno' for 'I don't know'.
Mockingbird\n\nA mockingbird is a bird that can sing many different songs. It copies the sounds of other birds, bugs, and frogs. It sings loud and fast. Mockingbirds live in warm places. They have gray feathers and a long tail.
North Macedonia\n\nNorth Macedonia is a country in Europe. It is on a big piece of land called the Balkan peninsula. The country has many mountains and lakes. The capital city is Skopje. People there speak Macedonian. Some people also speak Albanian. The money they use is called the denar. North Macedonia used to be part of a bigger country called Yugoslavia.
