Dvd\n\nA DVD is a shiny round disc. It looks like a CD but can hold more. You put it in a player to watch movies or shows on a TV. It spins around and a light reads the pictures and sounds inside. Many people have DVDs at home in a box or on a shelf.
Dwarf galaxy\n\nA dwarf galaxy is a tiny group of stars. It is much smaller than our big star home, the Milky Way. You can find it floating in space near bigger star groups. Sometimes it moves around a bigger galaxy, like the Moon moves around Earth. The Milky Way has many of these little star groups dancing around it.
Dwarf planet\n\nA dwarf planet is a round ball of rock or ice that goes around the Sun. It is smaller than a planet, but bigger than most space rocks. Some dwarf planets live in a far-away ring of rocks past Neptune. Others live in a belt of rocks between Mars and Jupiter. A dwarf planet has not pushed away all the other rocks near its path. One dwarf planet you might know is Pluto. It was once called a planet, but now it is a dwarf planet.
Dye\n\nDye is a colored liquid or powder that changes the color of things. It can be made from plants like berries, roots, or leaves. People also make it from special stuff in a factory. You put it on cloth to make a shirt red, blue, or yellow. It soaks into the cloth and stays there, even when you wash it. Some dye comes from nature, and some is made by people.
Dynamite\n\nDynamite is a strong boom-stick that people use to break big rocks. It looks like a soft, brown tube. Workers put it deep inside mountains or old buildings. When they light a long string, it goes BOOM and breaks the hard stone into small pieces. You might see it in a cartoon when a character runs away from a big blast.
Dynasty\n\nA dynasty is a family that rules a country for a long time. It is like a team where the leader's job passes from parent to child. You can find dynasties in old stories about kings and queens. They make big choices for the land and the people. A long time ago, many places had a dynasty, like old China or old Egypt.
E-mail\n\nE-mail is a letter you send on a computer or phone. It is like a paper letter, but it moves very fast through the Internet. You write words and can add a picture. It goes to a friend far away in just a few seconds. People use it to say hello, share news, or send a funny story. You need a special name, like a house address, to send it to the right person. Many people check their e-mail every day.
Each\n\nEach means every one in a group. It is a word we use when we talk about all the things or people, one by one. You might hear it when someone says, "Each child gets a cookie." That means every single child gets one. It helps us share fairly and make sure nobody is left out.
Eagle\n\nAn eagle is a big, strong bird that flies high in the sky. It has wide wings, a sharp hooked beak, and strong feet with claws called talons. You can find eagles in many places around the world, like mountains, forests, and near big lakes. It hunts during the day and has very good eyes to see small animals from far away. It catches food like fish or rabbits with its talons and uses its beak to tear the meat. An eagle is a meat-eater, so it only eats other animals.
Ear\n\nAn ear is a part of the body that helps you hear sounds. It has a soft outside part that you can see on the side of your head. Inside, there are tiny parts that catch sound and send it to your brain. People and many animals have two ears, one on each side. It also makes a sticky yellow stuff called earwax that keeps the inside clean. When you listen to a song or a friend talking, your ears are working hard.
Eared seal\n\nAn eared seal is a kind of seal that lives in the ocean. It has small ears you can see on the outside of its head. It uses its front flippers to push itself along on land. You can find it on rocky beaches or swimming in cold water. At the zoo or aquarium, you might see it clapping its flippers and barking loudly.
Earless seal\n\nAn earless seal is a big animal that lives in the sea. It has a round, smooth head with no ears you can see. It has a thick body and short flippers to swim fast. You can find it in cold ocean water near the top of the world. It comes onto land or ice to rest and have babies. A baby seal has soft white fur.
Early\n\nEarly means before the usual time. It is when something happens sooner than you think. You might wake up early in the morning when the sun is just coming up. If you get to school early, you are there before the bell rings. A flower that blooms early pops out before the other flowers. Being early can give you extra time to play or get ready.
Early childhood education\n\nEarly childhood education is a way to help young children learn and grow. It happens before kids turn eight years old. It takes place in places like preschools, daycares, and kindergartens. Teachers use songs, stories, and games to teach letters, numbers, and how to share. It helps children get ready for big school.
Early human migrations\n\nA long, long time ago, people moved from one big land to another big land. They walked very far to find new homes. They crossed land that is now under water. Some of them met other people who already lived there. Today, all people come from those first travelers.
Early Modern Period\n\nThe Early Modern Period is a big stretch of time in history. It came after the Middle Ages and before the time we live in now. During this time, people made new tools and sailed big ships to faraway lands. They also wrote many books and made beautiful art. You can see old things from this time in a museum, like shiny armor or old maps.
Earth\n\nEarth is the big round ball we live on. It is the third planet from the Sun. It looks blue and green from far away because it has lots of water and land. We find it in space, moving around the Sun. It is our home, and it gives us air to breathe, water to drink, and food to eat. You can see a small part of it when you look out the window or play outside.
Earth science\n\nEarth science is the study of our big home, the Earth. It looks at the ground, the water, the air, and even the sky above. It helps us know why the ground shakes, why it rains, and why the ocean has waves. People who do this work use tools to watch the weather and dig into rocks. They help keep us safe from big storms and find clean water to drink.
Earth's crust\n\nThe Earth's crust is the hard, rocky skin on the outside of our planet. It is like a giant eggshell, but much thicker under the land and thinner under the ocean. It is made of different kinds of rocks, and some of them are very old. The crust is broken into big pieces that move very, very slowly. When they bump into each other, they can push up tall mountains. You can see the crust when you look at a rocky hill or a cliff by the sea.
Earth's inner core\n\nEarth's inner core is a big ball of hot, hard metal at the very middle of our planet. It is made mostly of iron and nickel. It is so hot that it is as hot as the outside of the Sun. It is very, very deep under the ground, more than 5,000 kilometers down. The weight of everything above it pushes down so hard that the metal stays solid even though it is so hot. Scientists found out about it by listening to shakes from big earthquakes. The shakes move through the hard ball and tell us it is there.
Earth's magnetic field\n\nEarth's magnetic field is a big, invisible bubble around our planet. It acts like a giant shield that you cannot see. It is made deep inside the Earth, where hot, melted rock moves around. This bubble keeps away tiny, harmful bits that come from the sun. It also helps a compass point north, so people can find their way. Some birds and fish use it to travel far when the seasons change. Near the very top and bottom of the Earth, the bubble is strongest. Sometimes, the bubble even flips, so north becomes south and south becomes north, but that takes a very, very long time.
Earthquake\n\nAn earthquake is when the ground shakes very hard. It happens because big pieces of rock under the ground move and bump into each other. The shaking can make buildings fall down and things break. People use a special tool to see how strong the shaking is. Sometimes after a big shake, smaller shakes come later. If it happens under the ocean, it can make a giant wave that hits the land.
Earthworm\n\nAn earthworm is a small animal that lives in the dirt. It has a long, soft body with no legs and no eyes. Its body is made of many tiny rings. You can find it in wet ground, like in a garden or after rain. It digs tunnels in the soil, which helps plants grow. It eats old leaves and bits of dead plants. When it moves, it stretches and squeezes its body. It is good for the earth because it makes the soil soft and rich.
Earwig\n\nAn earwig is a small bug. It has a flat body and is dark brown or black. It has six legs and two long feelers on its head. At the back end, it has two little pinchers. It lives in wet, dark spots like under leaves or in old wood. Sometimes you see it in a bathroom or basement. It eats plants, fruit, and tiny bugs. It can give off a bad smell, so birds do not like to eat it.
Easily\n\nEasily means doing something without much work. It is like when you pick up a light toy, not a heavy box. You can find it in many things you do every day. For example, you can easily put on your shoes if they have no laces. It is also how a bird flies without thinking hard.
East\n\nEast is a direction. It is the way the sun comes up in the morning. If you face the sunrise, you are looking east. On a map, east is on the right side. Many birds fly east when the weather gets cold. Some people say, "The sun rises in the east."
East Africa\n\nEast Africa is a big part of the world. It is on the east side of a very big land called Africa. It has hot sun, tall grass, and big animals like lions and elephants. Long ago, the very first people lived there. Today, many people live in East Africa and speak many different words.
East Asia\n\nEast Asia is a big part of the world. It is in the east side of a huge land called Asia. Many countries are in East Asia, like China, Japan, and Korea. More than one billion people live there. They speak many different languages and eat yummy food like rice and noodles. You can see pandas in China and cherry flowers in Japan. East Asia has tall mountains and big cities with bright lights.
East China Sea\n\nThe East China Sea is a big body of water next to China. It is part of the huge ocean called the Pacific. It touches the land of China, Korea, Japan, and Taiwan. Many rivers flow into it, and the biggest one is the Yangtze River. Big boats sail on it to carry things from one place to another. People catch fish in it, and sometimes you can see it on a map as a blue shape near the land.
East Timor\n\nEast Timor is a small country on an island. It is in a warm part of the world near the big blue sea. It has many mountains and green hills. People live in towns and villages there. The biggest town is called Dili. A long time ago, people from far away came to live on the island. They grew food and fished in the sea. Today, people in East Timor speak their own words and also words from a place called Portugal. Children play in the sun and help their families.
Easter\n\nEaster is a happy spring holiday. It is a day when some people remember that Jesus came back to life. Many children get a basket with candy and chocolate eggs. They also look for eggs hidden in the grass by a bunny. The bunny is a make-believe friend who brings treats. People often wear new, bright clothes and go to church. Easter happens on a Sunday in March or April every year.
Easter Island\n\nEaster Island is a small piece of land in the big blue ocean. It has huge stone faces called Moai that stand near the sea. The faces were made long ago by people who lived there. The island also has a big round hole in the ground with a lake inside. Today, people live in a town called Hanga Roa. Many visitors come to see the stone faces.
Eastern\n\nEastern means the way where the sun comes up. It is one of the four main ways we look at a map. When you face the sunrise, you are looking east. Many places have the word East in their name, like East Coast. In stories, wise people sometimes come from the East.
Eastern Europe\n\nEastern Europe is a big part of the world with many countries. It is on the east side of Europe. People there speak different languages and have their own songs and stories. Some countries in Eastern Europe are Poland, Romania, and Bulgaria. Many families there cook warm soups and bread. In winter, it gets very cold and snow covers the ground.
Eastern Orthodox Church\n\nThe Eastern Orthodox Church is a big family of Christians. It has many beautiful buildings with round tops and gold crosses. You can find it in countries like Greece, Russia, and Serbia. People go there to pray, light candles, and sing songs about God. They also look at special pictures called icons that tell stories about Jesus and holy people.
Eastern Philosophy\n\nEastern philosophy is a way of thinking about big questions. It comes from places like China, India, and Japan. It asks things like: How should we live? What is real? It often talks about being calm, kind, and wise. Many people learn from it to feel peaceful inside.
Easy\n\nEasy means something is not hard to do. It is like when you put on your shoes all by yourself. You can find easy things everywhere, like a simple puzzle or a short walk. When a job is easy, it does not take much work or time. An example is picking up your toys when they are all in one spot.
Eat\n\nEat means to put food in your mouth, chew it, and swallow it. You do it when you are hungry. It helps your body grow big and strong. People eat many kinds of food like apples, bread, and rice. Animals eat too, like a bunny eating a carrot.
Eating\n\nEating is when you put food in your mouth and swallow it. It gives your body energy to run, play, and grow. People eat many kinds of food like fruits, meat, and bread. Animals eat too, but they eat different things. A cow eats grass, and a bird eats seeds. You eat breakfast in the morning, lunch at noon, and dinner at night. Eating together with family is fun.
Echidna\n\nAn echidna is a small animal with a long nose and sharp spikes on its back. It looks a little like a hedgehog. It lives in Australia and nearby islands. It digs a hole very fast with its strong claws to hide from danger. It eats ants and termites by catching them with its long, sticky tongue. A mother echidna lays eggs, which is very special for an animal with fur.
Echinoderm\n\nAn echinoderm is an animal that lives in the ocean. It has a body with five parts around a middle, like a star shape. You can find it on the sea floor, near the shore, or on reefs. It moves with tiny tube feet that fill with water. Some kinds are sea stars, sea urchins, and sea cucumbers. If it loses an arm, it can grow a new one.
Echo\n\nAn echo is a sound that bounces back to you. It happens when you yell in a big, empty room or near a tall mountain. The sound hits a hard wall or a rock and comes back to your ears. It sounds just like your voice, but a little softer and later. You can try it by clapping your hands in a quiet hallway.
Eclipse\n\nAn eclipse is when one big thing in the sky moves in front of another big thing. It happens with the Sun, the Moon, and the Earth. In a solar eclipse, the Moon blocks the Sun, and the sky gets dark for a short time. In a lunar eclipse, the Earth blocks the Sun, and the Moon looks red. You can see an eclipse if you look up at the right time, but you must wear special glasses to keep your eyes safe.
Ecology\n\nEcology is the study of how living things and their homes work together. It looks at plants, animals, and tiny bugs, and how they share food, water, and space. You can see ecology in a park, a pond, or even your own backyard. A bee visiting a flower is part of ecology. The flower gives food to the bee, and the bee helps the flower make seeds. All living things are connected like a big web.
Economic growth\n\nEconomic growth means people make more things and do more helpful jobs. It happens when workers build more houses, grow more food, or make more toys. Sometimes new tools and machines help them work faster. When there is more growth, families can buy more things they need. You might see a new shop open or a new road being built near your home.
Economic inequality\n\nEconomic inequality means some people have much more money than others. It is about how money and things are not shared the same way. Some families can buy a big house and lots of food, while other families have a very small place to live and not enough to eat. In some countries, the gap is very big, and in other countries, it is smaller. Grown-ups in charge try to make the gap smaller by helping people who have less.
Economic policy\n\nEconomic policy is the set of rules a country makes about money and jobs. It decides how much tax people pay and how the country spends its money. It also makes rules for banks and shops so things are fair. When the country builds a new road or school, that is part of its economic policy. It helps decide if things cost more or less at the store.
Economics\n\nEconomics is about how people choose to use things they have. It looks at how we make, share, and use food, toys, and other things we need. You see it at home when your family picks what to buy at the store. It also happens when a grown-up goes to work to earn money. The money helps pay for your house, your clothes, and your snacks.
Economy\n\nAn economy is how people make and share things we need. It has two parts: goods and services. Goods are things you can touch, like apples or shoes. Services are helpful things people do, like cutting hair or fixing a car. People use money to buy goods and services. Money makes it easy to trade. A long time ago, people traded one thing for another, like a chicken for a bag of rice. Today, we use coins and paper money. The word economy comes from an old word that means taking care of a home. Just like a family plans how to use food and toys, a big group of people plans how to make and share things.
Ecosystem\n\nAn ecosystem is all the living things in one place, like a forest or a pond. It has plants, animals, and tiny bugs that you cannot see. They all live together and need each other. A pond ecosystem has frogs, fish, and water plants. A desert ecosystem has cacti, snakes, and small animals that like dry sand. Every ecosystem needs sunlight so plants can grow. Plants make food from sunlight, and animals eat the plants or other animals. When the weather changes, the ecosystem can change too.
Ecuador\n\nEcuador is a small country in South America. It sits right on the equator, an imaginary line around the middle of the Earth. It has tall mountains called the Andes, green jungles, and a coast by the big Pacific Ocean. People grow bananas and cocoa there. The capital city is Quito, high up in the mountains. Many old, pretty buildings are in Quito. Far away in the ocean, it has islands with lots of animals like big turtles and funny birds.
Edda\n\nEdda is a very old book of stories. It tells about Viking gods and heroes from long ago. The stories were written down in a cold land called Iceland. People read it today to learn what Vikings believed. One story in it is about a strong god named Thor.
Edge\n\nAn edge is the sharp side of something. It is the part where two sides meet. You can find it on a table, a book, or a piece of paper. Sometimes it can cut you if you touch it, so you must be careful. A knife has a very sharp edge that helps it cut food.
Edison\n\nEdison is a famous man who made many new things. He lived a long time ago. He is best known for making the light bulb, which gives us light in our homes. He also made a machine that can record and play back sounds. Many people call him a great inventor because he never gave up trying.
Education\n\nEducation is learning new things. It happens when a teacher shows you how to do something, like reading or counting. You can find it at school, at home, or in a library. It helps you know more about the world. For example, when you learn to write your name, that is education.
Eel\n\nAn eel is a fish with a long, thin body like a snake. It has smooth skin and tiny scales you can hardly see. Most eels live at the bottom of the ocean, hiding in holes or sand. It hunts small fish and other sea animals for food. Some eels swim into rivers and lakes, so people can find it in fresh water too. A young eel is flat and see-through, and it looks very different from a grown-up eel.
Egg\n\nAn egg is a round or oval thing that a bird, a fish, or a bug makes. It has a hard or soft shell on the outside. Inside, a baby animal can grow until it is ready to come out. Many eggs are white or brown, but some are blue or green. People eat eggs from chickens for breakfast. You can cook an egg in a pan or boil it in water. A baby bird pecks the shell from inside when it is time to hatch.
Egypt\n\nEgypt is a big country in Africa. It has hot, sandy deserts and a long, long river called the Nile. Most people live near the river or the sea. Long ago, kings called pharaohs ruled Egypt. They built giant stone triangles called pyramids. You can still see them today. Many people visit Egypt to look at the pyramids and the big stone lion called the Sphinx.
Egyptian\n\nEgyptian means something from Egypt, a country far away with lots of sand and a big river. It can be a person who lives there, or things they make. Long ago, Egyptians built giant stone triangles called pyramids. They also wrote with little pictures. Today, people in Egypt speak a different language and live in busy cities.
Egyptian language\n\nThe Egyptian language is a very old way of talking and writing. It was used long ago in a place called Egypt. People wrote it with little pictures called signs. Some of these signs were cut into big stones. Today, almost no one speaks it every day, but a few people still use it in church. A big stone with three kinds of writing helped people learn to read the old signs.
Eid al-Adha\n\nEid al-Adha is a happy day for Muslim people. It is a time to share food and think about a very old story. In the story, a man named Ibrahim wanted to show he loved God more than anything. God saw his love and saved his son. Today, Muslim families remember this by giving meat to people who do not have much food. They also go to a big prayer together, wear new clothes, and give gifts to children. It is a day full of love and sharing.
Eiffel\n\nEiffel is a very tall tower made of iron. It stands in a big city called Paris, far away across the ocean. It looks like a giant metal triangle with three floors you can visit. People climb up inside it to see the whole city from high above. At night, it lights up with many tiny golden lamps. Many families take pictures next to it when they go on a trip.
Eiffel Tower\n\nThe Eiffel Tower is a very tall tower made of metal. It stands in a big city called Paris. It looks like a long, pointy triangle with three floors you can visit. People built it a long time ago for a big party. At night, many tiny lights on it sparkle and shine. You can ride an elevator up to the top and see the whole city below. It is one of the most famous towers in the world.
Eight\n\nEight is a number. It comes after seven and before nine. If you have eight crayons, you can count them: one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight. It looks like two circles, one on top of the other. You can see it on a clock, on a birthday cake, or in a book.
Eighteen\n\nEighteen is a number. It comes after seventeen and before nineteen. You can count to it with your fingers and toes. It is how old a person is when they become a grown-up in many places. You might see the number eighteen on a birthday cake with candles.
Einstein\n\nEinstein was a very smart man who thought about big ideas. He had wild white hair and a kind face. He lived a long time ago and worked with numbers and light. He helped people understand how the world works. You might see a picture of him sticking out his tongue in a funny way.
Either\n\nEither is a word we use when we talk about two things. It means you can pick one or the other, but not both. For example, at snack time, you might hear, "You can have either an apple or a banana." It helps us show that there are two choices.
El Dorado\n\nEl Dorado is a made-up city of gold. It is a place from old stories. People said it was hidden in South America. Long ago, some men from Spain looked for it. They wanted to find all the gold. But no one ever found it. It is just a story.
El Salvador\n\nEl Salvador is a small country in the middle part of the Americas. It has green hills, big volcanoes, and a long beach next to the big ocean. Many people live in towns and cities there. They speak Spanish and eat warm flat bread called tortillas. In the rainy time, it rains every day. In the dry time, the sun shines bright. Farmers grow corn and coffee beans on the land. El Salvador is so small that some people call it the "Tom Thumb" of the Americas.
Elastic\n\nElastic is a word that tells us something can stretch and then go back to its old shape. It is like a rubber band. You can pull it long, and when you let go, it snaps back small. Many clothes have elastic in the waist so they stay up on your body. A hair tie is elastic too. It stretches to hold your hair and then goes back when you take it off.
Elasticity (physics)\n\nElasticity is when something can stretch and then snap back to its first shape. It is like a rubber band. You pull it long, and when you let go, it goes back to being small and round. A spring in a toy also has elasticity. You push it down, and it jumps back up. Some things do not have elasticity. If you pull a piece of clay, it stays long and does not go back. Elasticity helps things like balls bounce and hair ties hold hair tight.
Elbow\n\nAn elbow is the bendy part in the middle of your arm. It lets you move your arm up and down and side to side. You can feel it when you touch the pointy bone on the back of your arm. It helps you eat, draw, throw a ball, and hug someone. When you bump it on something hard, it can feel funny and tingly.
Election\n\nAn election is a way for people to pick a leader. It is like a big group choice. You see it in towns and countries when people vote. They mark a paper or push a button to say who they want. Then the person with the most votes wins. It helps make fair rules for everyone.
Electric\n\nElectric is a kind of power that makes things work. It is like a hidden helper that moves through wires. You can find it in your house, in the walls and in cords. It makes lights turn on, the TV show pictures, and the fridge stay cold. When you flip a switch, it flows and does its job. A toy that needs batteries uses a tiny bit of it too.
Electric Battery\n\nAn electric battery is a small box that holds power inside. It can be round like a coin or long like a finger. You find it in toys, clocks, and remote controls. It makes things turn on and move without a cord. For example, a toy car uses a battery to zoom across the floor.
Electric charge\n\nElectric charge is a tiny thing that makes stuff pull or push. It lives inside every little piece of the world, like a secret power. You cannot see it, but you can feel it sometimes. When you rub a balloon on your hair, it picks up charge. Then the balloon can stick to the wall or make your hair stand up. That is because the charge makes things pull or push without touching. Sometimes you walk on a rug and touch a door, and you feel a tiny zap. That is charge jumping from you to the door. It is like a tiny, quick spark.
Electric current\n\nElectric current is a flow of tiny bits called charge. It moves through wires like water moves through a pipe. You can find it in the wires inside your house, in a battery that makes a toy light up, and in a big flash of lightning in the sky. It helps turn on lights, make fans spin, and power the TV. When you flip a switch, it flows and the room gets bright.
Electric eel\n\nAn electric eel is a long fish that lives in muddy rivers. It is not a real eel, but a kind of knifefish. It can make a strong zap, like a tiny bolt of lightning. It uses the zap to catch food and to stay safe from other animals. It lives in warm, slow rivers far away in South America. It must come up to the top of the water to breathe air. People almost never keep it as a pet because of its zap.
Electric field\n\nAn electric field is a special space around a thing that has electricity. It is like an invisible bubble that pushes or pulls on other electric things. You cannot see it, but it is there. When you rub a balloon on your hair, the balloon gets an electric field. It can make your hair stand up or stick to the wall. That is the field pulling on your hair.
Electric guitar\n\nAn electric guitar is a tool for making music. It has a long neck and a big round body. It uses six strings that you push down with your fingers. When you hit the strings, a small part called a pickup catches the sound and sends it through a wire to a loud box called an amp. The amp makes the sound big and loud. You can turn knobs on it to change how the sound feels. Many people play it in rock bands. You might see one on TV when a band plays a song.
Electric Light\n\nAn electric light is a thing that makes bright light when you turn it on. It has a glass bulb and a thin wire inside. You find it in houses, schools, and on streets. It helps people see when it is dark outside. A lamp on your desk is one kind of electric light.
Electric motor\n\nAn electric motor is a machine that makes things spin or move. It uses a hidden force called magnetism. Inside it has a part that can turn around and around. You find it in many things at home, like a fan, a washing machine, a fridge, and a vacuum cleaner. When you turn on a fan, the motor inside spins the blades fast to make wind. A long time ago, a man named Michael Faraday built the very first one with a nail, a wire, and a battery.
Electric power distribution\n\nElectric power distribution is how electricity gets to your house. It uses wires on tall poles or under the ground. Big metal boxes called transformers make the power safe to use. The power starts at a big station far away and travels through the wires. When you turn on a light, the power comes through these wires to make it shine.
Electric ray\n\nAn electric ray is a flat fish that lives in the sea. It has a round body and a long tail. It hides under the sand on the ocean floor. It can make a small zap of power, like a tiny shock. It uses this zap to catch food and to stay safe. Some people call it a torpedo ray.
Electrical engineering\n\nElectrical engineering is a job where people work with electricity. They think of new ways to use it to help us every day. They make things like lights, fans, and robots that can move on their own. They also fix broken wires and machines so they work again. You can find their work at home, in schools, and on the street. For example, the lights in your room and the TV you watch were made with help from electrical engineers.
Electrical generator\n\nAn electrical generator is a machine that makes power for lights and toys. It has wires inside that spin around very fast. When the wires spin, they make a kind of power called electricity. Some generators are small and you can turn them with your hand. Big ones sit in big buildings and use wind or water to spin. The power it makes can light up a room or make a toy move.
Electrical grid\n\nAn electrical grid is a big web of wires that brings power to your house. It starts at a power plant where electricity is made. Then it travels on tall towers and poles across long roads and fields. The wires go to a small box near your home and then into the walls. When you turn on a light or the TV, it sends the power to make it work. It works all day and night so we can have light, heat, and fun.
Electricity\n\nElectricity is a kind of power that moves through wires. It is like a hidden helper that makes things work. You cannot see it, but it is inside the walls of your house. It turns on lights so you can see at night. It makes the TV show your favorite shows. It keeps the fridge cold so food stays fresh. When you flip a switch, it flows to a lamp and the room gets bright. A battery has a little bit of it inside to make toys move. It can be very strong, so never touch a plug with wet hands.
Electricity generation\n\nElectricity generation is the way people make power. It is the force that turns on lights, runs fridges, and makes toys move. Most of it comes from big machines that spin very fast. These machines burn things like black rocks or gas to turn. Some use wind or falling water to spin. A different way uses flat shiny panels that catch sunlight and turn it right into power. You can see these panels on some house roofs. The power then travels on long wires to your home. When you flip a switch, the light goes on because of this power.
Electromagnet\n\nAn electromagnet is a special kind of magnet that works only when electricity flows through it. It is made of a wire wrapped many times around a piece of metal, like an iron nail. You can find it inside many things at home, such as a doorbell or a toy motor. When you turn on the electricity, it becomes a magnet and can pick up small metal things like paper clips. When you turn off the electricity, it stops being a magnet and lets go. It is different from a fridge magnet, which always sticks.
Electromagnetic\n\nElectromagnetic is a big word for a kind of push and pull that you cannot see. It is like a hidden force that can move things without touching them. You can find it in magnets that stick to the fridge. It also makes lights turn on and helps your TV show pictures. A good example is when you rub a balloon on your hair and it sticks to the wall.
Electromagnetism\n\nElectromagnetism is a force that pushes and pulls tiny bits called charges. It has two parts: an electric part and a magnetic part. You can see it when you rub a balloon on your hair and the balloon sticks to the wall. It also makes magnets stick to the fridge. It is all around us, even though we cannot see it.
Electron\n\nAn electron is a tiny, tiny piece of stuff that is part of everything around us. It is so small you cannot see it, even with a big magnifying glass. It lives in atoms, which are like tiny building blocks for all things. It moves around the center of the atom, like a bee buzzing around a flower. When many electrons move together, they make electricity, which turns on lights and makes your TV work.
Electronic commerce\n\nElectronic commerce is buying and selling things using a computer or phone. It happens on the internet. You look at pictures of toys, books, or clothes on a screen. Then you click to pick what you want, and a grown-up pays with a card. Later, a box comes to your door with the thing inside. Many people shop this way because it is fast and easy.
Electronic dance music\n\nElectronic dance music is music made with computers and special machines. It has a strong beat that makes people want to move their bodies. You hear it at parties, clubs, and sometimes on the radio. A DJ plays it by mixing different sounds together. It can be fast and happy, or slow and dreamy. Some songs have singing, and some have only sounds. When you hear it, you might jump, spin, or wave your arms.
Electronic music\n\nElectronic music is music made with special machines. It uses computers and boxes with buttons to create sounds. You can hear it on the radio, in movies, or at a dance party. People make it by pressing keys or turning knobs, and the machine makes a beat or a melody. Sometimes it sounds like a robot singing or a funny beep-boop noise.
Electronics\n\nElectronics is a way to use tiny bits of power to make things work. It uses small parts that let power flow or stop it. You find it inside many things at home, like a TV or a toy that lights up. It helps a screen show pictures and a speaker make sound. When you press a button and a toy moves or sings, that is electronics at work.
Element\n\nAn element is a basic kind of stuff that everything is made of. It is like a tiny building block that you cannot break into smaller pieces. You can find elements all around you, like the air you breathe and the water you drink. Some elements are shiny metals, and some are invisible gases. For example, the shiny yellow metal called gold is an element, and the air you blow out is made of elements too.
Elephant\n\nAn elephant is the biggest animal that lives on land. It has a very long nose called a trunk and big, floppy ears. Its skin is thick and wrinkly, and it has big, strong legs. Some elephants have long, white teeth called tusks that stick out from the mouth. Elephants live in hot places like Africa and Asia. They walk in big family groups and talk to each other with low sounds we cannot hear. An elephant uses its trunk to pick up food, drink water, and give itself a shower. It eats grass, leaves, and branches. A baby elephant is called a calf and stays inside its mom for almost two years before it is born. You can see an elephant at the zoo or in a picture book.
Elevation\n\nElevation is how high a place is. It tells us if a place is up high or down low. We measure it from the top of the ocean, which is flat and still. Most land is higher than the ocean, so it has a plus number. A few dry places are lower than the ocean, so they have a minus number. A tall mountain has a big elevation. A flat beach has a small elevation.
Elevator\n\nAn elevator is a small room that moves up and down. It has walls, a floor, a ceiling, and doors that slide open and shut. You find it inside tall buildings, like stores or apartments. People step in, push a button, and it carries them to a different floor. It helps people who cannot use stairs, like someone in a wheelchair. When you ride in one, you feel a little push as it starts and stops.
Eleven\n\nEleven is the number after ten. It is one more than ten. You can see it on a clock, on a calendar, or when you count your toys. When you have ten blocks and add one more, you have eleven blocks. It is a number that comes before twelve.
Elijah\n\nElijah is a person from very old stories. He was a man who spoke for God. He wore a long coat and lived a long time ago. In one story, he asked God to send fire from the sky, and it came down. In another story, he helped a woman whose son was sick, and the boy got better. People remember him as a brave helper.
Elizabeth\n\nElizabeth is a name for a girl or a woman. It is a long name with three parts: E-liz-a-beth. Many people with this name are called Liz, Beth, or Eliza for short. You might know a friend, a teacher, or a storybook character named Elizabeth. Some queens in old times also had this name.
Ellipse\n\nAn ellipse is a shape that looks like a squashed circle. It is round but longer one way and shorter the other. You can see it in a mirror that is not round, or in a plate that is not a perfect circle. The path a planet takes around the sun is an ellipse. You can draw it by tying a string to two pins and pulling a pencil around them.
Elm\n\nAn elm is a tall tree with many green leaves. It has a thick brown trunk and branches that spread out wide. You can find it in parks, forests, and along streets in many places. Its leaves have little teeth along the edges and a pointy tip. In the fall, the leaves turn yellow or brown and fall to the ground. The tree makes small flat seeds that spin in the wind like tiny wings. It grows very slowly and can live for a long, long time.
Else\n\nElse is a word we use when we talk about another thing or a different choice. It means something that is not the first thing we said. You might hear it when someone says, "Do you want an apple or something else?" It helps us ask about more things or pick a new thing. When you play a game and one rule does not work, you can try something else.
Email\n\nAn email is a letter you send using a computer or a phone. It goes from one person to another person very fast, like magic. You write words on a screen and press a button to send it. It can have a picture or a file attached to it. People use it to say hello, share news, or ask a question. You need an email address, which has an @ sign in the middle.
Embarrassment\n\nEmbarrassment is a feeling you get when you think you did something silly in front of other people. It can make your face feel hot and turn red. Sometimes you might smile a little or want to hide your face. It happens when you trip and fall, or when someone says something nice about you and you don't know what to say. It is a normal feeling that everyone has sometimes.
Embroidery\n\nEmbroidery is a way to make cloth look pretty with colored thread. It uses a needle to sew little lines and shapes. You can find it on shirts, hats, or blankets. People use it to draw flowers, letters, or animals on fabric. Some grown-ups learn it in a class and then teach others. A grandma might stitch a name on a towel as a gift.
Embryo\n\nAn embryo is the very first stage of a baby animal or a new plant. It is so tiny you cannot see it without a special tool. It starts from one small cell that grows and splits into many cells. In people, it stays inside the mom's belly for about eight weeks before it gets a new name. After that, it grows bigger and looks more like a baby. All animals and plants begin as an embryo before they are born or pop out of a seed.
Emerald\n\nAn emerald is a shiny green stone. It is very pretty and people wear it on rings or necklaces. It comes from deep under the ground. People dig it up and cut it to make it sparkle. It is the color of fresh grass in spring. Some emeralds are light green and some are dark green. It is one of the most special stones in the world.
Emergency department\n\nAn emergency department is a special room in a hospital. It is the place where people go when they are very sick or hurt and need help right away. It has doctors and nurses who work all day and all night. They help people who come in a fast car with a loud siren, called an ambulance. Sometimes people call it an emergency room, or ER for short. You might see one on a TV show where doctors run to help someone who just got hurt.
Emergency medical services\n\nEmergency medical services are helpers who come fast when someone is very sick or hurt. They ride in a big van called an ambulance. It has a loud siren and bright lights so cars move out of the way. Inside, they have beds and tools to help people breathe and stop bleeding. They take care of you right where you are and then bring you to a hospital if you need more help. You might see an ambulance on the street when you hear a loud wee-woo sound.
Emotion\n\nAn emotion is a feeling inside you. It can be happy, sad, angry, or scared. You feel it in your body, like a smile when you are happy or tears when you are sad. All people have emotions, and so do animals like dogs and cats. A dog wags its tail when it is happy to see you. Emotions help you know what you need, like a hug when you are sad.
Empathy\n\nEmpathy is a feeling that helps you know how another person feels inside. It is like putting your heart next to someone else's heart. When a friend is sad, you feel a little sad too. When a friend is happy, you feel happy with them. It helps you be kind and share. You can show it by giving a hug or saying a soft word. It makes people feel safe and loved.
Emperor\n\nAn emperor is a person who is the boss of a very big land. He wears a shiny crown and sits on a big chair called a throne. Long ago, many countries had an emperor. He tells people what the rules are. You can see an emperor in a storybook or a movie about old times.
Empire\n\nAn empire is a very big group of lands and people all ruled by one leader. It is like a giant kingdom that has many smaller parts. Long ago, empires grew by taking over faraway places. Some empires moved across the land with horses and soldiers. Other empires used big ships to sail across the sea and find new lands. You might see pictures of old empires in storybooks about kings, queens, and brave explorers.
Empire State Building\n\nThe Empire State Building is a very tall building in New York City. It has 102 floors and many windows. People go inside and ride an elevator way up high. From the top, they can see the whole city. At night, it lights up with pretty colors. It is one of the most famous buildings in the world.
Empty\n\nEmpty means there is nothing inside. A cup with no water is empty. A room with no people is empty. When you eat all your food, your plate is empty. It is the opposite of full.
Emu\n\nAn emu is a very big bird that cannot fly. It has a long neck, long legs, and soft brown feathers. It lives in Australia, in open places with grass and trees. It runs very fast on its strong legs to find food like seeds, flowers, and bugs. A daddy emu sits on the eggs to keep them warm until the babies hatch. The babies have stripes on their feathers to hide in the grass.
Enceladus\n\nEnceladus is a giant from very old Greek stories. He is big and strong, much taller than any person. In the stories, he lives under a mountain on an island. When he moves, the ground shakes and the mountain makes loud noises. Some people say that is why we have earthquakes and volcanoes. He is one of many giants in those old tales.
Encryption\n\nEncryption is a way to hide a message so only the right person can read it. It is like a secret code. You change the words into a jumble of letters that look like nonsense. Only someone with a special key, like a password, can turn the jumble back into the real words. When you send a note to a friend, you can use a simple code. For example, you might change each letter to the next one in the alphabet. Then "HELLO" becomes "IFMMP". Your friend knows the trick and can change it back. On computers, encryption keeps your secrets safe when you play games or send messages.
Encyclopedia\n\nAn encyclopedia is a big book or a website full of facts. It has many pages about different things, like animals, stars, or how cars work. You can find it at a library or on a computer at home. People use it to learn new things or look up answers. For example, if you want to know why the sky is blue, you can look in an encyclopedia.
End\n\nAn end is the last part of something. It is where a thing stops. You find it at the finish of a book, a movie, or a line. When you reach it, there is no more after that. For example, the end of a race is when you cross the finish line.
Endangered species\n\nAn endangered species is a kind of animal or plant that may soon be gone forever. It has very few of its kind left in the world. You can find some of them in special parks or safe places that people made to help them. People make rules to keep it safe, like no hunting and no breaking its home. A big cat called a tiger is one animal that is endangered.
Energy\n\nEnergy is the power that makes things move, light up, or get warm. It is like an invisible helper that is everywhere. You can see it when the sun shines, when a ball rolls, or when a light turns on. It can change from one kind to another, like when you eat food and then run and play. It never goes away; it just moves or changes shape.
Engine\n\nAn engine is a machine that makes things move. It takes energy and turns it into motion. You can find it inside a car, a train, a boat, or a plane. It helps the vehicle go from one place to another. Some engines burn fuel like gas to make power. Others use electricity from a battery. A toy car with a battery has a tiny engine inside it.
Engineer\n\nAn engineer is a person who builds and fixes things. She uses tools and thinks of new ideas. You can find her at a building site, a bridge, or a factory. She makes cars, roads, and tall towers. When a toy breaks, an engineer can help put it back together.
Engineering\n\nEngineering is using science and math to make new things. People who do this job are called engineers. They learn how to build and fix things at a big school. They work with many other people to make big things like bridges, cars, and computers. Some engineers make tall buildings, and some make toys that move. They think hard to solve problems and help everyone.
England\n\nEngland is a country with many people. It is part of a bigger group called the United Kingdom. The flag of England is white with a red cross. The biggest city is London, and many people live there. England has green hills, old castles, and a long river called the Thames. A long time ago, kings and queens lived in big stone houses. Today, people in England speak English, just like you and me.
English\n\nEnglish is a way people talk and write. It uses letters like A, B, and C to make words. Many people in the world speak English. You can hear it on TV, in songs, and in stories. When you say "hello" or "thank you," that is English. It helps people from different places talk to each other.
English Channel\n\nThe English Channel is a big stretch of water. It sits between the country of Great Britain and the rest of Europe. On a clear day, you can see from one side to the other at its thinnest part. People cross it on big boats called ferries. They can also ride a train that goes under the water in a long tunnel. Some strong swimmers have crossed it by swimming for many hours. In France, people call it by a different name.
English language\n\nEnglish is a way people talk and write. It started long ago in a country called England. Now many people all over the world use it. You can hear it in songs, see it in books, and watch it in movies. When you say "hello" or "thank you," you are using English. It has 26 letters, like A, B, C, and so on. Some words sound the same but look different, like "two" and "too." People in America, England, and many other places speak it every day.
English literature\n\nEnglish literature is stories, poems, and plays written in the English language. It can be a book you hold in your hands or words someone reads out loud. You find it in libraries, schools, and at home on a shelf. People read it for fun, to learn new things, or to hear a good tale. A bedtime story your mom or dad reads to you is a small piece of English literature.
Engraving\n\nEngraving is a way to cut a picture or words into a hard, flat thing. It uses a sharp tool to scratch lines into metal, wood, or stone. You can find it on pretty jewelry, shiny cups, or the metal plates that print money. People use it to make special pictures on paper or to decorate things like rings and watches. The lines it makes are smooth and stay there for a very long time.
Enjoy\n\nEnjoy means you feel happy when you do something. It is like a warm, smiley feeling inside. You can enjoy eating a yummy snack, playing with a toy, or listening to a story. When you enjoy something, you want to do it again and again. It makes your heart feel light and your face show a big grin.
Enki\n\nEnki is a very old god from long-ago stories. He was the god of water and knowing things. People said he made two big rivers flow. He was also linked to a bright star in the sky and a picture of a man pouring water. Sometimes he was shown as a goat-fish, which has a goat head and a fish tail. Today, we see him in star signs: the water pourer and the goat-fish.
Enlightenment\n\nEnlightenment is a big word for a time when people learned to think in new ways. It happened long ago in places like Europe. People started to ask many questions about the world. They used their own minds to find answers, not just old books. This helped them make new tools and share big ideas. It was like a bright light turning on in a dark room.
Enough\n\nEnough means you have all you need. It is when your tummy is full after a meal, or when you have just the right number of blocks to finish your tower. You do not need more and you do not have too little. When you feel happy and not wanting, that is enough.
Entertainment\n\nEntertainment is something fun that makes you happy. It can be a game, a show, a song, or a story. You find it on TV, at a park, or in a book. It helps you laugh, smile, and forget about sad things. A cartoon you watch is one kind of entertainment.
Envelope\n\nAn envelope is a flat paper pocket. It has a flap that you can fold down and stick shut. You put a letter or a card inside it. Then you write a name and address on the front and put a stamp in the corner. The mail carrier takes it to the person you want to reach. You might see an envelope when you get a birthday card in the mail.
Environmentalism\n\nEnvironmentalism is caring for the world around us. It means keeping the air, water, and land clean and safe. People who care about this are called environmentalists. They do things like putting paper and cans in special bins to use again. They also try to use less water and turn off lights to save power. Some of them help plant trees and pick up trash in parks. They want to make sure the Earth stays a happy home for all living things.
Epic poetry\n\nEpic poetry is a very long story told like a song. It has brave people who go on big trips and do hard things. Long ago, people told these stories out loud before books were made. One old story is about a strong man named Beowulf who fights a monster. Today, some writers still make new epic poems.
Epidemic\n\nAn epidemic is a sickness that spreads to many people in a big place. It moves from one person to another very fast. Doctors work hard to stop it with medicine and shots. When it spreads to many countries, it is called a pandemic. Washing hands and staying home can help keep people safe.
Epilepsy\n\nEpilepsy is a problem in the brain. It makes a person shake or move in a way they cannot control. This shaking is called a seizure. A seizure can be short or long. Some people take special medicine to help stop the seizures. A doctor can help find the best way to care for a person with epilepsy.
Episode\n\nAn episode is one part of a longer story. It is like a small piece of a big puzzle. You can watch an episode on TV or a tablet. Each episode tells a little part of the story, and when you watch many episodes, you learn the whole story. For example, your favorite cartoon has many episodes, and each one is a new adventure.
Epistemology\n\nEpistemology is a big word for thinking about how we know things. It asks questions like: how do you know the sky is blue? You see it with your eyes. How do you know a lemon is sour? You taste it. It is the study of what we know and how we learn. People use it when they ask if something is true or not.
Equal\n\nEqual means two things are the same in some way. It can be about size, like when two blocks are just as tall. It can be about number, like when you and a friend each have three cookies. In a game, equal turns mean everyone gets the same chance to play. When you share a snack, you try to make the pieces equal so it is fair.
Equality\n\nEquality means everyone gets the same fair chance. It is like sharing a big cookie so each friend gets a piece just the same size. At school, it means all kids can play together and learn together. At home, it means brothers and sisters take turns with toys. When people are equal, no one is left out or treated better just because of how they look or where they come from.
Equation\n\nAn equation is a math sentence. It has numbers and a sign that looks like two lines on top of each other. That sign means both sides are the same. You can see it in a school book or on a board. It helps you know how much something is. For example, 2 plus 3 equals 5 is an equation.
Equator\n\nThe equator is an imaginary line around the middle of the Earth. It is not a real line you can see, but it helps us on maps. It splits the Earth into a top half and a bottom half. Places near it are very hot and wet all year. They do not have cold winters like other places. You can find it on a globe as the line that goes around the fattest part.
Equatorial Guinea\n\nEquatorial Guinea is a small country in Africa. It has land on the big part of Africa and also on islands. One big island is called Bioko, and the main city is there. Many people speak Spanish because long ago Spain was in charge. It is near the ocean, so you can see water and boats. The land has green trees and hot weather.
Equestrianism\n\nEquestrianism is a sport where people ride horses. It has many different games and ways to ride. Some riders jump over tall fences while a clock ticks. Others make the horse dance in soft sand with no jumps at all. You can see it at big shows or on a farm. A child might ride a pony at a fair or watch a horse race on TV.
Equilibrium\n\nEquilibrium is when things are balanced and stay the same. It is like a seesaw that does not tip up or down. You can find it in a glass of water that is not moving. It also happens when you mix colors and they stop changing. A toy car sitting still on a flat floor is in equilibrium.
Equinox\n\nAn equinox is a special day that happens two times every year. On this day, the sun shines straight over the middle of the Earth. It makes day and night almost the same length. One equinox comes in spring, when flowers start to grow. The other comes in fall, when leaves turn red and yellow. Long ago, people had happy parties on these days.
Era\n\nAn era is a long, long stretch of time. It is like a big chapter in a storybook about the world. People use it to talk about times when things were very different from today. For example, when dinosaurs walked the Earth, that was a different era. When your grandparents were little, that was another era. An era can last for many, many years.
Erase\n\nErase means to make something go away. When you use a pencil, you can rub the marks off with a rubber eraser. It makes the paper clean again. You can also erase words on a whiteboard with a cloth. Sometimes people erase a drawing to start over. It helps fix mistakes.
Eraser\n\nAn eraser is a small soft thing that takes away pencil marks. It is often pink or white and feels a little bit like rubber. You can find it on the end of a pencil or as a block in a pencil box. When you make a mistake with a pencil, you rub it over the mark and the mark goes away. After you use it, little bits of it fall off, so you need to brush them away.
Eris (dwarf planet)\n\nEris is a big ball of ice and rock far away in space. It is round like a ball and very cold. It lives past all the big planets, way out in the dark. It moves around the sun, but it takes a very long time—more than 500 years. It has one small moon that goes around it. You cannot see it from your backyard because it is too far. Scientists use big telescopes to look at it.
Eritrea\n\nEritrea is a country in Africa. It is next to the Red Sea, a big body of water. It has neighbors called Sudan, Ethiopia, and Djibouti. The land is not very big. Many people there speak a language called Tigrinya. The capital city is Asmara, where many people live. Long ago, different countries ruled the land. Now it is its own country. People from Eritrea are called Eritreans. They have many different groups with their own ways and languages. Some people grow food or take care of animals. The weather is often hot and dry.
Erosion\n\nErosion is when wind, water, or ice slowly wears away rocks and dirt. It happens outside on the ground. Rain can wash soil down a hill. Wind can blow sand into big piles. A river can cut a deep path in the land over many years. This is how canyons are made. It can also make the ground less good for growing food.
Erupt\n\nErupt means to burst out suddenly. It is like when a volcano throws out hot, melted rock and ash. You can see it in pictures of a mountain with red and orange stuff flying up. It can also mean a loud, sudden noise, like when a crowd cheers all at once.
Especially\n\nEspecially means more than other things. You use it when one thing is the most important. If you say, "I like all fruits, especially apples," it means apples are your favorite. You can also say, "Be careful, especially near the stove," to show the stove is the most dangerous part. It helps people know what to pay the most attention to.
Espionage\n\nEspionage is when someone tries to find out secrets. It is like hiding and watching to learn things that are not for everyone to know. A person who does this is called a spy. A spy might look at papers, listen to talks, or take pictures without asking. In a war, it is against the rules to do this. Sometimes a spy works for one side, and sometimes they work for two sides at once.
Essay\n\nAn essay is a piece of writing that shares what a person thinks. It is made of words on paper or a screen. You find it in school, in books, or on the computer. A student writes it to tell ideas about one big topic. For example, a child might write about their favorite animal and why they love it.
Estonia\n\nEstonia is a small country in Europe. It sits next to the Baltic Sea. Its land has many trees, lakes, and little islands. The biggest city is Tallinn. People there speak a language called Estonian. They sing and dance at big song parties. In winter, the ground gets cold and white with snow. Many birds live there, like storks and eagles. A long time ago, it was part of a bigger country, but now it is free and has its own flag.
Estuary\n\nAn estuary is a place where a river meets the big sea. It has water that is a little salty and a little fresh. The river gets wide and slow there. You can see tall grass, small crabs, and many birds. It is a safe home for baby fish before they swim to the deep ocean.
Ethics\n\nEthics is about what is good and what is bad. It helps people think about the right way to act. When you share your toys, that is good. When you push a friend, that is bad. Ethics is like a set of rules for being kind and fair. It is used in many places, like at home, at school, and in the whole world.
Ethiopia\n\nEthiopia is a big country in Africa. It has tall mountains, green hills, and a long history. Many people live there, and they speak different languages. A long time ago, it was called Abyssinia. Today, you can find old stone churches and busy markets in its cities. Children in Ethiopia play games and help their families, just like you do.
Ethnicity\n\nEthnicity is a big word for the group of people your family comes from. It can mean sharing the same language, food, or stories from long ago. Some people have light skin, some have dark skin, and that can be part of ethnicity too. You might see different ethnicities at your school or in your neighborhood. Everyone's ethnicity is special, like a piece of a big, colorful puzzle.
Etiquette\n\nEtiquette is a set of rules about how to be nice and polite. It tells you what to do when you eat, talk, or play with others. You learn it at home, at school, and from watching grown-ups. For example, saying "please" and "thank you" is good etiquette. It can be different in different places, but it always helps people get along.
Etymology\n\nEtymology is the study of where words come from. It looks at how words change over time and what other languages they came from. You can find etymology in big books called dictionaries. It helps us understand why words sound the way they do. For example, the word "etymology" itself comes from old Greek words that mean "true word."
Eucalyptus\n\nEucalyptus is a kind of tree. It has long, thin leaves that smell strong and fresh. Most of these trees grow in Australia, where it is warm. The bark can be smooth or rough, and it often falls off in strips. People use the leaves to make oil that helps with coughs and colds. Some animals, like koalas, eat the leaves because they can handle the strong taste. The tree grows very tall, and its wood is used to build things.
Eukaryote\n\nA eukaryote is a tiny living thing made of small parts called cells. It has a special bag inside the cell that holds its instructions. You can find eukaryotes all around you—plants, animals, and mushrooms are all eukaryotes. It can be just one cell, like the green stuff on a pond, or many cells, like a dog or a tree. When you look at a leaf or a bug, you are looking at a eukaryote.
Euphrates\n\nThe Euphrates is a very long river. It flows through hot, dry lands in a place called the Middle East. Long ago, people used its water to grow food and build big cities. Today, big walls called dams hold back some of the water. It joins another river called the Tigris, and together they go into a big sea.
Eurasia\n\nEurasia is a very big piece of land. It is made of two parts: Europe and Asia. It has water all around it. The Atlantic Ocean is on one side, and the Pacific Ocean is on the other. It is the biggest piece of land on Earth. Many people live there, and it has many countries.
Eurasian eagle-owl\n\nThe Eurasian eagle-owl is a very big bird that flies at night. It has big round eyes, a hooked beak, and two pointy tufts on its head that look like ears. It lives in rocky places, near woods and water, in a big part of the world called Eurasia. It hunts small animals when it is dark outside. It makes a deep hooting sound that you can hear far away.
Eurasian magpie\n\nA Eurasian magpie is a black and white bird. It has a long tail and shiny dark feathers that can look blue or green in the sun. It lives in many places like Europe and Asia. It builds a big round nest high up in a tree. It eats small animals, eggs, and bits of food people leave behind. You might see it hopping on the grass in a park.
Eurasian Steppe\n\nThe Eurasian Steppe is a very big, flat land with lots of grass. It has no trees, just wide open fields. You can find it far away in places like Russia and China. Long ago, people rode horses across it to travel from one side of the world to the other. It was like a big road made of grass. Many different groups of people lived there and moved around with their animals.
Euro\n\nEuro is the money that many countries in Europe use. It comes as paper bills and round coins. You can see it in shops when people buy food or toys. One euro can be split into 100 tiny parts called cents. The bills have different colors and pictures of old buildings. The coins have one side that is the same everywhere, and the other side shows a picture from the country that made it. If you visit France or Spain, you can use the same euro coins and bills.
Europa (moon)\n\nEuropa is a big moon that goes around the planet Jupiter. It is a little smaller than our own Moon. Its outside is made of ice and is very flat and smooth. It has long lines and cracks on top. Scientists think there is a big ocean of water hiding under the ice. The water stays warm because Jupiter pulls on it. A man named Simon Marius found it a long time ago. He gave it the name Europa, after a girl from an old story.
Europe\n\nEurope is a big piece of land with many countries. It has water on three sides: a big ocean to the west, a cold ocean to the north, and a warm sea to the south. Many people live there, and they speak different languages. You can see old castles, tall mountains, and busy cities. Some children in Europe eat bread and cheese for breakfast.
European badger\n\nA European badger is a furry animal that digs tunnels under the ground. It has a white face with two wide black stripes over its eyes. It lives in the woods and fields across Europe. It sleeps in a cozy room inside its tunnel during the day and comes out at night to find food. It eats worms, bugs, fruit, and small plants. It keeps its home very clean and makes a special spot for its poop. Sometimes it lets other animals like rabbits share its tunnel. It is usually calm, but it can fight hard if it feels scared.
European honey bee\n\nA European honey bee is a small, busy insect that makes sweet honey. It has a fuzzy body with yellow and black stripes, six legs, and two see-through wings. It lives in a big group called a hive, which you can find in trees or in wooden boxes that people build. It flies from flower to flower to sip a sweet juice called nectar, which it turns into honey inside the hive. When one bee finds good flowers, it does a little wiggle dance to tell the other bees where to go. People keep these bees so they can collect the honey to eat on bread or in tea.
European robin\n\nA European robin is a small bird with a bright orange-red chest and face. It has brown wings and a white belly. You can find it in gardens, parks, and woods in many parts of Europe. It hops on the ground looking for bugs and worms to eat. It sings a pretty song, especially in the morning. In winter, it may come close to people digging in the dirt, hoping to find a snack.
Evaporation\n\nEvaporation is when water turns into air that you cannot see. It happens when water gets warm. You can see it when a puddle on the ground gets smaller on a sunny day. The water goes up into the sky and hides in the air. Wind and sun make it go faster. It is part of how rain comes back down later.
Even\n\nEven means things are the same size, amount, or number. When you share cookies with a friend and you both get the same number, that is even. It can also mean a number you can split into two equal groups, like 2, 4, or 6. You can see even when you cut a sandwich into two equal halves. It is the opposite of odd or lopsided.
Evening\n\nEvening is the time of day when the sun goes down and the sky gets dark. It comes after afternoon and before night. You can see the colors in the sky change to orange, pink, and purple. People eat dinner in the evening and get ready for bed. The moon and stars start to shine.
Event\n\nAn event is something that happens. It can be a big party, like a birthday with cake and balloons. It can also be a show, like a play or a concert. People plan events so friends and family can come together and have fun. Sometimes an event is outside, like a fair with games and rides. You might go to an event at school, like a sports day or a holiday show.
Ever\n\nEver is a word that means at any time. It is a small word you hear in questions and stories. You might ask, "Have you ever seen a rainbow?" That means, "Did you see a rainbow at any time in your life?" It can also mean always, like in "I will love you forever." That means for all time, without end. You hear it in songs and books when people talk about big feelings.
Everglades\n\nThe Everglades is a big, wet, grassy place in Florida. It is a slow river that looks like a wide, flat swamp. Many animals live there, like birds, fish, and big reptiles. People visit it to see the animals and the water. It is a park that keeps the land and animals safe.
Every\n\nEvery means all of something. It is a word we use when we talk about each one in a group. If you eat every cookie, there are no cookies left. If you hug every friend, you hug all of them. Every day means all the days, one after the other.
Everybody\n\nEverybody means all the people. It is a word you use when you talk about every single person in a group. When the teacher says "everybody, line up," she means all the boys and girls. At a birthday party, everybody gets a piece of cake. It is a happy word because it means no one is left out.
Everyone\n\nEveryone means all the people in the world. It is a word we use when we talk about every single person. When you look around, you see many faces, and everyone has a smile, a name, and a family. At school, everyone plays together at recess. At home, everyone sits at the table for dinner. It is a big word that holds all of us.
Everything\n\nEverything means all things. It is the whole world, every person, every animal, every toy, and every star in the sky. When you look around, you see a little bit of everything. It is a big word for all there is. You cannot hold everything in your hands because it is too big. But you can think about it when you look up at the night sky full of stars.
Everywhere\n\nEverywhere means all places. It is not one spot but the whole world around you. You can find air everywhere, because air is in your room, outside, and even up in the sky. Love is also everywhere—you feel it at home, at school, and with friends. When you look up, the sky is everywhere above you.
Evil\n\nEvil is when someone does something very bad on purpose. It is not a thing you can touch, but you can see it in mean actions. You might see it when a person hurts another person or breaks something just to be unkind. In stories, a witch or a monster is often evil. It is the opposite of good.
Evolution\n\nEvolution is how living things slowly change over a very long time. It is why there are so many different plants and animals today. You can see how it works by looking at old bones in rocks, called fossils. They show that animals from long ago look different from animals now. For example, a horse from long ago was as small as a fox and had many toes. Over time, it grew bigger and now has one big toe on each foot. This change happened bit by bit, over millions of years.
Exactly\n\nExactly means something is just right, with no mistake. When you put a puzzle piece in the right spot, it fits exactly. If you ask for three cookies and get three, that is exactly what you wanted. It is like a key that turns in a lock with no wiggle room.
Examination\n\nAn examination is a test that checks what you know or can do. It has questions you must answer. You see it at school when your teacher gives you a paper with questions. It helps the teacher see how much you learned. Sometimes it is not on paper but on a computer. A doctor also does an examination by looking at your body to see if you are sick. When you do well, you pass and feel proud.
Example\n\nAn example is one thing that shows what other things are like. It helps you understand something new. A teacher might say, "Here is an example of a circle," and point to a round clock. When you learn colors, a red apple is an example of red. It makes learning easy and fun.
Excite\n\nExcite is a big, happy feeling. It is when you jump up and down because something fun is about to happen. You might feel it on your birthday or when you see a big present. It makes your heart beat fast and your smile grow wide. You can also feel it when you go to the park or see a friend. It is a feeling that makes you want to shout, "Yay!"
Excited\n\nExcited is a feeling you get when something very good is about to happen. It makes your heart beat fast and your body feel jumpy. You might smile a lot, clap your hands, or even shout with joy. You can feel this way before a birthday party, when you see a new toy, or when you go to the park. It is a happy, bouncy feeling that makes you want to move and laugh.
Exciting\n\nExciting is a feeling you get when something big or fun is about to happen. It makes your heart beat a little faster and you might smile or jump up and down. You can feel it on your birthday, before a trip, or when you open a present. It is like a happy buzz inside you.
Excretion\n\nExcretion is how the body gets rid of waste it does not need. It happens in people and animals every day. When you go pee, that is excretion. When you breathe out, you push out a gas called carbon dioxide. Your skin also helps by making sweat. All these ways keep the body clean and healthy inside.
Executive (government)\n\nThe executive is a group of people who run a country every day. It is like the boss of the country's helpers. It does not make new rules—that job is for another group. It does not decide what rules mean—that is for judges. Instead, it makes sure rules are followed. The leader of the executive is often called the president or prime minister. This leader picks other helpers to take care of things like schools, hospitals, and talking to other countries. You can see the executive on TV when the leader gives a speech or visits a school.
Exercise\n\nExercise is when you move your body to stay strong and healthy. It can be running, jumping, or playing outside. You can do it at the park, in your yard, or even inside your house. It makes your heart beat faster and your muscles grow. When you play tag with friends, that is exercise.
Expensive\n\nExpensive means something costs a lot of money. A big toy or a shiny bike can be expensive. You need many coins or bills to buy it. Sometimes a thing is expensive because it is hard to make or very special. A small candy is not expensive, but a big cake can be. When Mom says a toy is too expensive, it means we cannot buy it today.
Experience\n\nExperience is something you learn by doing or seeing. It is not from a book, but from trying things yourself. When you ride a bike for the first time, you get experience. You might fall, but then you learn how to balance. Watching a friend do something also gives you a little experience. It helps you know what to do next time.
Experiment\n\nAn experiment is a way to test an idea. It is like a game where you try something to see what happens. You can do it in a lab with tools, or just in your head. It helps people learn if an idea is right or wrong. For example, if you think a toy car goes faster on a smooth floor than on a bumpy rug, you can try it and watch. That is an experiment.
Explain\n\nTo explain is to tell someone about something so they understand it better. It uses words, hands, or pictures to show what you mean. A teacher explains a new game to the class. A friend explains why they are sad. When you explain, you help someone see what you see.
Exploration\n\nExploration is when people go to new places to learn about them. It is like a big adventure where you find things you did not know before. Long ago, people sailed on big boats across the ocean to find new lands. They also walked on land with animals like camels to see what was far away. Today, people explore space in rockets to learn about stars and planets. You can explore too, like when you look under a rock in your yard and find a bug.
Explore\n\nExplore means to look around and find new things. When you explore, you walk and see what is there. You can explore a park, a big room, or your own backyard. It is like going on a small trip to learn about a place. Sometimes you find a pretty rock or a bug under a leaf. Exploring helps you know the world better.
Explorer\n\nAn explorer is a person who goes to new places to see what is there. He travels far away, sometimes over big water or tall mountains. He may find new lands, animals, or plants that no one saw before. He uses a map and a compass to know where he is going. A long time ago, explorers sailed on big boats to find new parts of the world. Today, some explorers go deep under the sea or high up into space.
Explosive\n\nAn explosive is a thing that can go BOOM very fast. It can break rocks or make a big loud noise. People use it to dig tunnels through mountains. Fireworks are a kind of explosive that make pretty colors in the sky. You should never touch an explosive because it can hurt you.
Exponentiation\n\nExponentiation is a way to multiply a number by itself many times. It uses a small number up high to show how many times. You can see it in math class on a board. It helps people count big numbers fast. For example, two with a small three means two times two times two, which is eight.
Expressionism\n\nExpressionism is a way of making art. It is not about showing things exactly as they look. Instead, the artist uses colors and shapes to share a big feeling. You can find it in paintings, plays, and music. The colors might be wild and the shapes might be bent. A famous painting called The Scream shows a person with a very scared face. That painting helps you feel the same fear.
